# Current state — jpegxl-rs

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

_(none)_

## Constraints

### Correctness order: conformance before performance

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.correctness-before-speed/1` · scope `all` · topic `correctness-order`

Work proceeds in this order of priority: conformance, resource safety, memory
ownership, scalar performance, parallelism, SIMD, then encoder quality search.

### Correctness is measured by pixels, not byte-parity with libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.correctness-metrics/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/**"` · topic `correctness-metrics`

Decoder success is not lossless correctness. Conformance compares parse success,
dimensions, bit depth, color interpretation, frame count, an exact pixel hash for
lossless paths, and peak error plus RMSE for conforming lossy paths. Byte-for-byte
parity with libjxl is not a general target.

### The decoder enforces explicit resource limits

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.decoder-resource-limits/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `resource-limits`

The decoder enforces explicit, configurable upper bounds and validates all TOC
ranges before allocating or launching workers.

### Start forbidding unsafe; add SIMD unsafe only with a local contract

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.forbid-unsafe-by-default/1` · scope `all` · topic `unsafe-policy`

Crates start with forbid(unsafe_code). Unsafe SIMD is added only after profiles show
a concrete bottleneck and only where the safety contract is local and documented.

### No runtime dependency on libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.no-libjxl-runtime-dep/1` · scope `all` · topic `no-libjxl-dep`

The shipped library has no runtime dependency on libjxl or any C JPEG XL codec.
External decoders are invoked only as separate processes by the conformance harness.

### Parsers use checked arithmetic and never panic on bad input

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.constraint.no-panic-checked-arith/1` · scope `all` · topic `no-panic`

Every parser operation uses checked arithmetic and enforces resource limits.
Invalid or unsupported syntax returns a typed error; it never panics and never
silently substitutes defaults.

## Policies

### Clean-room: no architectural port of libjxl

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.clean-room-boundary/1` · scope `all` · topic `clean-room`

This is a native, standard-first Rust implementation. Implement from ISO/IEC 18181
and legitimately obtained specifications, never by porting libjxl architecture or
code. libjxl and other decoders are validation oracles only.

### Test count is not confidence; unknown coverage stays unknown

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.coverage-honesty/1` · scope `all` · topic `coverage-honesty`

Do not equate the number of tests with confidence, and do not claim conformance
coverage that has not been demonstrated against the corpus. Unknown profile and
feature coverage must be recorded as unknown, not assumed.

### E.4.4 ICC tag dictionary has 17 entries; use the LaTeX

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.e44-tag-dictionary/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `e44-tag-dictionary`

The E.4.4 tag dictionary has 17 entries (tagcode range 4..=20), including bTRC and
dmda. part1.md truncates it to 15 (OCR dropped those two). Use the LaTeX source;
confirmed by byte-exact fixtures.

### Encoder heuristics are not normative; keep them out of the syntax model

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.encoder-analysis-separate/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `encoder-analysis`

Keep encoder analysis (predictor evaluation, MA-tree construction, context
clustering, palette/RCT/Squeeze selection, LZ77 matching, block/quant search)
separate from the decoder-visible syntax model. A decoder-visible MaTree is
normative data; the algorithm that discovers it is not. Do not let an encoder
heuristic become a decoder requirement.

### EXPERIMENT_CLAMP_SYMMETRIC = false is not a loosened check

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.h52-clamp-asymmetric/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"` · topic `h52-clamp`

Keep the asymmetric H.5.2 clamp (EXPERIMENT_CLAMP_SYMMETRIC = false). Do not
restore the printed symmetric clamp "to match the spec".

### jpxl bench isolates Modular and VarDCT encode paths

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.jpxl-bench-entry-points/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `jpxl-bench-entry-points`

Profile Modular and VarDCT separately. The CLI encode path is Modular only; a
flamegraph of jpxl encode does not describe VarDCT.

Measurement modes via release jpxl bench:
- modular: Modular lossless (MA search, residuals, LZ77, entropy, bit writing)
- vardct-fixed: VarDCT fixed quantizer (transform selection, transforms, CfL,
  quantize, emit; no rate-loop multiplication)
- vardct-rate: VarDCT target rate (full exact-price rate loop)
- vardct-probe: one predetermined quantizer plan+emit

Optional --input path.ppm (8-bit RGB P6) replaces the synthetic RGB pattern.
Output fields: wall_ms_total, wall_ms_median, output_bytes, and an FNV-1a
fingerprint for cross-iteration identity. Promote to a baseline only under
@jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules (crypto hashes of binary and stream,
decode gate, size classes); FNV alone is not enough for promotion.

### modular_16bit_buffers = false for >8-bit encodes is deliberate

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.modular-16bit-buffers/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `modular-16bit-buffers`

For >8-bit encodes, modular_16bit_buffers = false is deliberate: it is a truthful
claim about decoder working buffers (D.3), and its paired consequence is the jxll
level-10 box in container output (Annex M). Do not restore the Table D.3 default.

### Modular residual LZ77 must use H.3 dist_multiplier

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.modular-lz77-dist-multiplier/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-decode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"` · topic `modular-lz77-dist`

The residual SymbolDecoder must be given set_dist_multiplier(max_channel_width).
Encode distances as raw = distance + 119 when M > 0 (C.3.3 past the special table),
never raw = distance - 1 as if M = 0. Do not "fix" round-trip failures under full
modular decode by forcing M = 0 on the decoder.

### Correctness gates by optimization change type

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.optimization-correctness-gates/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"` · topic `optimization-gates`

Gate each optimization class before merge: bulk bit writer, plan Arc-sharing,
flat coefficient arena, and scratch reuse require byte-identical codestreams;
Rayon section encoding requires byte-identical results across thread counts;
integer SIMD requires scalar-versus-SIMD byte identity; floating DCT
factorization or SIMD requires decode validity plus the declared Contract A or
B; search pruning or approximate prices requires size/quality/target adherence
and an exact final-price gate; LZ77 algorithm changes require byte equality if
tie rules are preserved, otherwise equal or better exact stream size. Validate
with the in-project decoder and libjxl (oracle process). Decode time is not
included in encode timing.

### Pass oracle output format explicitly; do not loosen the PPM parser

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.oracle-output-format/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/**"` · topic `oracle-output-format`

jxl-oxide ignores the output-file extension and writes PNG bytes into any filename.
Pass --output-format explicitly. Do not "fix" a BadMagic PPM parse error by
loosening the PPM parser; the harness rejects PPM-from-jxl-oxide before spawning
(OracleError::UnsupportedFormat).

### Clean-room boundary and version pinning for the in-tree perceptual metric

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.perceptual-metric-clean-room/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-plan-render/**"`

The in-tree metric in jpxl-perceptual is derived only from the public SSIMULACRA2 specification/README (cloudinary/ssimulacra2) and, for cross-checking, the BSD-2-Clause rust-av `ssimulacra2` crate already present as an optional measurement dependency. libjxl's tools/ssimulacra2.cc and any other file under libjxl/ are not derivation sources. The metric's defining constants (scale count, components, map families, Gaussian sigma, SSIM constants, the 108-term aggregation shape, final weights and remap) are part of the metric's public definition and may be reproduced; the implementation (blur recurrence, layout, parallel banding, reductions) is JPXL's own. jpxl-encode-policy never depends on jpxl-perceptual, jpxl-plan-render or jpxl-decode as a normal dependency; it sees only a PerceptualEvaluator trait and the facade injects the implementation. jpxl-plan-render never calls jpxl-decode; shared leaf kernels live in jpxl-core and each tree keeps its own reconstruction orchestration, guarded by parity against jpxl-decode, djxl and jxl-oxide. The rust-av crate remains a dev/test parity oracle only and never enters the production path. The metric version string, the pinned test-vector fingerprint and the measured score guard are recorded with the metric; changing any of them is an encoder-behaviour change requiring a Contract B screen.

**derived_from** `@jpegxl-rs.policy.clean-room-boundary/1`

### Promoted performance baseline rules

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules/1` · scope `path "JPXL/**"` · topic `performance-baseline-rules`

A number is a promoted performance baseline only when all of the following hold;
otherwise it is a scratch or diagnostic measurement and must not be treated as a
baseline claim:

1. Immutable binaries: hash every binary involved; recheck before every timed run
   and reject the run if the hash changed.
2. Pinned inputs: exact image, its hash, dimensions, bit depth, and color encoding.
3. Interleaved A/B, never separate batches; report minimum, median, and dispersion.
4. Correctness gate alongside timing: output bytes and hash, and decoded-pixel
   result. A fast wrong answer is not a datum.
5. Host state: thread count, CPU affinity and policy, load, free memory, swap and
   tmpfs use, competing jobs. Measurements under resource pressure are diagnostics
   only, never baselines.
6. Cache regime stated: cold-cache, warm-cache, and warm-process are distinct;
   never merge them.
7. Size classes: at minimum a small (~4 MP) and a large (≥12 MP) image.
8. Unknown stays unknown: if profiling explains 48% of samples, report 48% and
   label the rest UNKNOWN.

Profile Modular and VarDCT separately. The CLI encode path is Modular-only; a
flamegraph of jpxl encode does not describe VarDCT. On hybrid Intel hosts, prefer
an explicit userspace P-core event (cpu_core/cycles/u) and verify that the folded
period total equals the perf event total before trusting an SVG.

### Prefer the LaTeX and image scans over OCR transcriptions

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.prefer-latex-over-ocr/1` · scope `all` · topic `source-of-truth`

For normative constants and algorithms, prefer the LaTeX transcription and, when in
doubt, the image scan, over OCR-derived markdown (part1.md and similar). Do not
re-transcribe values from a source already known to be corrupted; cite the verified
source in the record that carries the value.

### Keep research metrics and benchmarks out of the codec core

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.research-out-of-core/1` · scope `all` · topic `research-separation`

The codec core carries no research metrics, perceptual scoring, or benchmark
scaffolding (for example Butteraugli belongs to encoder development tooling, not the
decoder). The changelog is not a research database. Durable measurement summaries
and baseline rules live in AKR; full raw run logs and flamegraph artifacts live
under .agent/scratch/ (not pruned by akr build). Frozen experiment writeups may
go in JPXL/docs/experiments/ when a self-contained report is warranted.
JPXL/docs/PERFORMANCE.md is a stub only, not the measurement store.

### The encoder writes RestorationFilter explicitly OFF

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.restoration-filter-off/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `restoration-filter`

The encoder writes RestorationFilter explicitly OFF (gab = false, epf_iters = 0)
rather than relying on the Table J.1 defaults (gab = true, epf_iters = 2), because
those defaults are decoder-side smoothing our decoder does not implement yet. If
external decodes drift while self-roundtrip stays green, look here first.

### Register outside advice; track adoption and completion only in AKR

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.sources-advice-completion/2` · scope `all`

External architecture and optimization advice is registered through the AKR source library and stored under sources/external with an immutable content hash. Top-level intake copies and Markdown status sidecars are removed after registration; AKR planning records are the only progress and completion surface. Do not rewrite advice into a checklist or parallel plan. A registered full source may be finalized only through the source-library workflow when its durable citations and metadata have been retained.

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.policy.sources-advice-completion/1`

### When every transcription agrees on nonsense, suspect the pipeline

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.suspect-transcription-pipeline/1` · scope `all` · topic `transcription-pipeline`

When every transcription agrees on nonsense, suspect the transcription pipeline,
not the standard. Escalate to the image scan before claiming a standard defect.

## Observations

### Prevalidated inline ANS slot lookup is byte-identical with a small consistent wall gain; retained

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.ans-slot-lookup-2026-09-01/1`

On the working tree atop 45d948630dec1bac11bc98e6a9ea727e33c2e2a8 plus the retained trailing-truncation change, replacing the once-per-symbol checked AnsEncodeTable::slot call in the backward rANS pass with an inline slot_prevalidated lookup (safe by construction: new re-checks the C.2.6 bijection and the pass's zero-mass gate plus state%p bound the indices; the public checked slot remains for every other caller) was byte-identical across the full 32-encode matrix (two anchors, quality/rate, t1/t4, default/scalar; canonical large-anchor hashes matched). Two independent 12-repetition pinned ABBA matched-rate screens against the truncation-only binaries never showed a slower cell across 48 paired reps; pooling both runs (24 paired reps per cell, ans-pooled.txt) gives medians 0.9954, 0.9856, 0.9900, 0.9916, with large-12MP t4 excluding 1.0 at CI95 [0.9748,0.9981] and the other three cells' upper bounds at or just above 1.0. Peak RSS was unchanged in both runs. The realizable gain is around 1%, at the harness's ~0.5% resolution floor, consistent with the frontier's prediction that the 3.99% checked-lookup share would only partially convert; both runs again carried large clock drift, so the paired intervals carry the verdict. Retained: byte-identical, no memory cost, no regression signal, and a statistically excluded interval on the anchor hosting the largest ANS share.

### At matched bitrate our single-pass activity AQ field is a net perceptual loss: off beats every tuning tried, on both metrics

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.aq-field-is-a-net-perceptual-loss-2026-08-10/2`

The adaptive-quantization field, as tuned and as shipped, is a net PERCEPTUAL LOSS at matched bitrate. Turning it off improves both perceptual metrics.

Method: sweep the field's three constants at a FIXED bitrate and score each result with jpxl compare. Fixed-rate because AQ does not change how many bits are spent, only where, so the honest question is "at the same file size, which allocation looks better". Driver and raw output in .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/aq-sweep.ps1 and aq-sweep-0p8MP-{1,2}bpp.txt. `strength = 0` produces a neutral field, which AqSetup treats exactly as AqMode::Off, so that row IS "AQ disabled".

small_0p8MP at 1.0 bpp (bytes, ssimulacra2 higher-better, butteraugli lower-better):
AQ OFF (strength 0) -- 98141, 59.378, 6.075. Shipped (0.25/1.0/0.35) -- 97769, 59.617, 6.636.
Every other config tried: strength 0.10 (6.710), 0.40 (6.776), 0.60 (6.732), 1.00 (6.633); clamp 0.5 (6.781), 2.0 (6.583); chroma 0.0 (6.756), 1.0 (6.784).

small_0p8MP at 2.0 bpp:
AQ OFF -- 196459, 81.971, 3.185. Shipped -- 195444, 80.007, 3.562.
Every other config: ssimulacra2 79.64-80.01, butteraugli 3.447-3.828.

Two things stand out. First, AQ-off is not the end of a trend -- it is an OUTLIER. Every non-zero strength, every clamp and every chroma weight clusters tightly (butteraugli 6.58-6.78 at 1 bpp, 3.45-3.83 at 2 bpp) while AQ-off sits well outside it. So this is not "the strength constant is mistuned"; it is that having a non-neutral field at all costs perceptual quality here. Second, the penalty does not shrink as the rate rises -- at 2 bpp AQ-off is better on BOTH metrics (+1.96 ssimulacra2 and -10.6% butteraugli), where at 1 bpp it was better on butteraugli (-8.4%) and marginally worse on ssimulacra2. That rules out the obvious explanation of the per-varblock HfMul signalling row eating the coefficient budget, which would fade as a fraction of a larger file.

A likely reason it was never caught: M7's acceptance evidence (jpegxl-rs.evidence.m7-adaptive-quant) reads "spatial quality uniformity improved with stable target size". Uniformity is what AqMode::Uniform optimises -- busy atoms finer, error equalised. Production ships the opposite direction, AqMode::Masking (busy atoms coarser), whose case is perceptual masking and which the uniformity criterion does not test. So the shipped direction was accepted on a criterion the other direction satisfies, and no perceptual metric existed in this repository to check it against until now.

INTERPRETATION, sharpened by cross-project evidence (jpegxl-rs.observation.bpg-rs-aq-precedent-2026-08-10/2): this field is a SINGLE-PASS ACTIVITY field, and that is the class that also busted in bpg-rs, where two-pass measured AQ pays 3-10% but every single-pass mode did not. So the right reading is not "AQ does not pay here" but "this KIND of AQ does not pay here, and retuning its constants cannot fix it because the signal is the problem". NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and this should not become a default flip until it is: one image, two rates, one host. Untested are the other two corpus images, other rates, AqMode::Uniform (which would separate "this direction is wrong" from "the machinery costs quality regardless of direction"), and any non-photographic content, where masking is most likely to earn its keep. The measurement infrastructure to settle all of that now exists (EncodeRequest::budget.aq_tuning, `jpxl encode --aq-strength/--aq-clamp/--aq-chroma`, `jpxl compare --features perceptual`).

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.observation.aq-field-is-a-net-perceptual-loss-2026-08-10/1`

### AQ precedent from bpg-rs: two-pass measured AQ pays 3-10%; every single-pass activity mode busted -- and ours is single-pass

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.bpg-rs-aq-precedent-2026-08-10/2`

Cross-project precedent from the sibling still-image codec at D:\\Rust-projects\\bpg-rs (still265, HEVC lineage), on which kinds of adaptive quantization pay and which do not.

THE SPLIT THAT MATTERS: two-pass *measured* AQ works there -- 3-10% gains. Every single-pass mode was a bust. That distinction, not "AQ good/bad", is the transferable lesson.

Source note and a correction to an earlier draft of this record: an automated read of that repository's git history, docs and ledger found no committed number crediting AQ, and this record initially concluded there was no payoff. That was wrong. The two-pass result is known directly from the project's author; the harness (scripts/aq_experiment.py) writes bdrate_vs_uniform.csv / equal_byte_deltas.csv and those output files were never committed, which is why a repository-only read could not see them. Absence of a committed CSV is not absence of a result -- a reminder that a repo read is evidence about the repo, not about what was measured.

What busted there, and is visible in the history: the initial default-on per-CU variance AQ (commit d87aee7) was backed out a day later (6fc5dae) -- "the per-CU variance AQ on the speed tiers hurt quality and scrambled the ladder" -- and the same commit set AQ off by default. The docs record the single-pass activity attempts as "neutral-to-negative on photos" and "not the main photo-gap lever" (docs/ssimtune.md:325). The AqMode enum's other single-pass variants (LegacyShrink, Perceptual, PerceptualChroma, PsnrProbe, PositiveProbe) were likewise not adopted.

What works there: AqMode::TwoPassMeasured (commit fec6680). Pass 1 encodes and measures per-quantization-group *coded coefficient energy*; pass 2 redistributes QP from that measurement. An A/B over candidate signals -- coefficient energy vs rd(D+lambda R) vs SSE vs bits -- found coefficient energy "wins decisively". A three-pass candidate-compare gate gives it a safety property: it encodes a uniform-QP pass too, compares at equal bytes, and reverts to uniform when AQ would lose, so "two-pass AQ can improve a picture but never regress one".

Also on record there, unchanged by the correction: the "~3%" in commit 6fc5dae is the whole-encoder BD-rate gap against x265 m9, not an AQ figure, and that commit turned AQ off. Sign-data hiding was a separate, clean equal-bytes win (~+0.05 dB, 15-20% of the measured gap) and was promoted to default. AQ-active configs are forced out of the WPP parallel fast path, so AQ costs throughput as well as effort.

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE, and it is not what it first appeared. Our field (jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs) is a SINGLE-PASS ACTIVITY field: log2(1+variance) per 8x8 atom against the frame mean, luma plus down-weighted chroma, x265-family strength and clamp. That is precisely the class that busted in bpg-rs -- and jpegxl-rs.observation.aq-field-is-a-net-perceptual-loss-2026-08-10 independently measures ours to be neutral-to-negative on photos at matched bitrate, the same verdict. Two codecs, different transforms, different metrics, same result for the same class of method.

So the conclusion is NOT "AQ does not pay". It is: single-pass activity AQ does not pay, and no amount of retuning our three constants will change that, because the signal is the problem. If AQ is ever revisited here it should be built as two-pass measured -- measure coded coefficient energy per group in pass 1, redistribute in pass 2, and gate it against a uniform-QP encode at equal bytes so it cannot regress. That is a substantial build, it multiplies encode cost in a codec already 58-530x slower than cjxl, and it is explicitly deferred until the speed and rate-loop problems are fixed.

Scope limit: evidence about one other implementation's experience, and one of the numbers in it is reported rather than read from a file.

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.observation.bpg-rs-aq-precedent-2026-08-10/1`

### Current-HEAD profiles reproduce the perceptual closure and expose an exact base-encoder frontier

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.current-head-quality-rate-profile-2026-09-01/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/src/restoration.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/src/encode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/src/**"`, `path "JPXL/tools/quiet_ab.py"`

At HEAD 45d948630dec1bac11bc98e6a9ea727e33c2e2a8, fresh `cpu_core/cycles/u` profiles on the locked 12 MP photo, pinned to the six physical P-cores at t6, reproduce the perceptual-kernel closure but expose a separate exact base-encoder frontier. Quality captured 30,212 samples: horizontal_band_avx2 14.29%, epf_step_rows_fma 10.80%, vert_batch_avx2 10.22%, planes_to_positive_xyb_avx2 6.97%, and accumulate_band_avx2 4.63% (46.91% combined), with no new large perceptual instruction defect. The current quality trace is 3 pixel probes / 2 exact prices and 433 ms plan + 1350 ms render/metric + 90 ms entropy + 115 ms emit; each pixel probe is 422-489 ms, so avoiding one remains the only double-digit wall lever and requires the already-identified Contract B policy choice. The matched-rate profile captured 8,861 samples and finds three exact candidates outside that closure: (1) truncate_trailing's two monomorphizations are 2.56%+2.43% inclusive and their per-call Vec collections are 2.26%+2.20%; a reverse nonzero cursor can preserve decisions while removing per-varblock allocation and the post-Y full refresh scan. (2) walk_pass_group<CensusSink> is 7.13% and the later trained-tape record walk is 5.48%; retaining packed raw (pre-context,value) events during census would allow sequential replay after hybrid-uint training, replacing the second coefficient/context traversal for about 24.6 MiB at the final plan's 3,223,433 symbols. (3) AnsEncodeTable::slot is a non-inlined checked Result-returning lookup at 3.99% of rate cycles and 0.99% of quality cycles; the self-built TokenTape path can use a separately validated inline lookup while generic callers retain errors. These shares are ceilings, not measured wins. Raw profiles, exact commands, hashes, trace, diagnostics, caveats and ranking are kept in .agent/scratch/frontier-refresh-20260901/.

### The cover/CfL objective misprices Y-channel error by 2.65x across DCT8x8 frequency; the mispricing is in the ruler, not the lever

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.distortion-currency-misprices-frequency-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/tests/perceptual_frequency.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`

block_cost_bounded prices every candidate as J = bits + lambda_c * side^2 * sum_cells (recon - target)^2: a flat sum of squared dequantized-coefficient errors with one scalar lambda per channel, calibrated once at the DCT8x8 operating point. Cell (0,1) and cell (7,7) are charged identically for the same error magnitude.

Phase 6.0 measured what that unit actually costs perceptually, with no encoder in the loop. For each XYB channel and each DCT8x8 cell, equal coefficient energy was injected into every whole 8x8 block of a real photograph with a deterministic per-block sign, converted back to 8-bit sRGB, and scored against the unperturbed round trip. Equal injected energy means the current objective charges every cell the same, so the measured spread is the missing weighting directly. Control: realized sample-domain SSE varied only 8.2% across cells (8-bit clipping) against a 165% perceptual spread, so the result is perception and not basis energy.

Y channel, 63 non-LLF cells, normalised so the flat objective is 1.00 everywhere: range 0.68 to 1.80, a 2.65x spread. Every one of the fifteen pairwise Pearson correlations between normalised maps -- across two photographs at 0.8 MP and 4 MP, over a 4x amplitude range -- is r >= 0.961, reaching r = 0.997 between the two images at amplitude 1.0. The shape is a band-pass contrast-sensitivity curve peaking at the lowest non-DC frequencies ((1,1) = 1.80, (1,0) = 1.79, (0,1) = 1.77), falling to about 0.70 mid-high, with a mild corner re-rise ((7,7) = 0.83). X has a similar shape but saturates (2.35x, r 0.488 to 0.871; its own standard deviation is about 0.0025, so amplitude 1.0 is far outside any real operating point). B is close to flat and unstable (1.56x, r -0.057 to 0.951): for B the current objective is approximately right and no weighting is justified.

This is a mechanism for the measured gap split -- 25-37% behind cjxl on PSNR, 12-20% on SSIMULACRA2, 39-53% on butteraugli. The encoder is closest on the metric its own objective is. It also explains the Phase 5J/5K/5L/5M/5N/5O pattern: six different levers, one unchanged scorer, scattered content-dependent results. No lever can compensate for a mispriced ruler.

What this does NOT establish, recorded because the temptation to skip to a weight table is the whole risk. (1) It does not show a re-weighted objective improves output, only that the current one is mispriced: HfQuantizer::choose picks the nearest reconstruction level rather than an RD-optimal one, so a weight changes cover and CfL selection and nothing else until quantization itself becomes RD-aware. (2) DCT8x8 only; the cover decision compares transforms of different sizes and each size has its own frequency grid, so applying this table to that comparison without a per-transform model would bias selection in a new direction rather than remove the existing bias. (3) Row and column 4 are a consistent local minimum with a partial re-rise at 5-7 -- a first-principles CSF has no such feature and butteraugli's multi-scale pyramid plausibly does, which is a direct argument against fitting the numbers literally. (4) Clean-room (AGENTS.md section 2): measuring a black-box metric's response is the same category as running cjxl/djxl as an oracle and reads no libjxl source, but the workspace manifest's own note on the butteraugli dependency applies exactly -- fitting an encoder weight table to this response would make the perceptual model a derivative of libjxl's, whereas deriving a first-principles contrast-sensitivity weight and then checking it against this measurement would not.

Suggested continuation, in dependency order. 6.1 (cheapest and most decision-relevant, should run before any weight is written): real quantization injects error proportional to each cell's quantization step, and the standard's default dequant matrices (F.3/I.5) are themselves perceptually shaped. Re-run injecting error proportional to HfQuantizer::step. If the response flattens, the matrices already carry the weighting and the objective's only mistake is measuring in dequantized rather than quantizer-normalised units -- a one-line fix with a large effect. If it does not flatten, the residual is the real target. 6.2: extend to DCT16x16 and DCT32x32 so the cover comparison can be re-priced coherently. 6.3: a first-principles CSF weight, checked against this table rather than fitted to it, behind a feature flag, screened on the six-scene matrix under the existing Contract B promotion rules.

Full tables, stability matrix and method: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-distortion-currency-frequency-response.md. Raw output: .agent/scratch/phase6-0-frequency-response-2026-08-12/.

### The standard's own DCT8x8 matrix donates the best frequency weight yet: a large low-rate win fading to a no-op by 4 bpp, which points at the quantizer

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.donor-weight-wins-at-low-rate-and-fades-2026-08-12/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/csf.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`

OPTION 1 IS CLOSED, AND CLOSING IT EXPLAINS PHASE 6.3. The canonical DCT-domain per-coefficient models -- Ahumada & Peterson (1992), Peterson, Ahumada & Watson (1993), Watson's DCTune (1993), Nill (1985) -- are all detection-threshold models: band-pass with a low-frequency dip and a high-frequency rolloff HARDER than Mannos-Sakrison. AP92 predicts about 0.037 of peak sensitivity at Nyquist where measurement says about 1.05, roughly 28x off against Mannos-Sakrison's 3.1x, so adopting any of them would be strictly worse than what 6.3 already rejected. Georgeson & Sullivan (1975) supply the reason: above threshold, perceived contrast becomes largely independent of spatial frequency (contrast constancy), so a detection CSF -- which describes seeing a grating on a blank field -- is the wrong regime for judging quantization error in real content, where low-frequency error is highly visible. That is why the measured curve has no low-frequency dip.

THE CANDIDATE. The I.2.5 default dequantization matrices are a distortion allocation rather than a detection threshold. Scored against the measured target, 1/step^2 from the DCT8x8 matrix gives median 1.41x, against the CSF's 2.06x and a 1.18x ceiling for a curve fitted directly to butteraugli -- so it captures most of the available improvement without fitting to the metric, and option 3 was not pursued. But using each size's own matrix does NOT work: that is the 1/step^2 weighting Phase 6.2 already falsified, because the matrices are per-size tuned and their step shapes disagree 3.34x across sizes against the measured curve's 1.15x. Reading ONE size's matrix as a curve in normalised radial frequency and resampling it onto every transform's grid repairs that by construction. Which size donates was settled by measurement: DCT8x8 1.43x, DCT16x16 1.90x, DCT32x32 2.62x, geometric mean of all three 2.34x -- averaging is worse than DCT8x8 alone because the steeper 16/32 curves drag it off target.

TWO GATING CORRECTIONS, both needed to read Phase 6.3 fairly. Its 1.35x worst-bin tolerance was unachievable by its entire model class: the best smooth two-parameter shape FITTED to the target cannot beat 1.72x worst-bin, so that gate measured only that a smooth curve cannot reproduce two artifact bins. And worst-bin is dominated by f below 0.1 and above 0.9, so median is the primary statistic and worst-interior the secondary.

AGREEMENT GATE PASSES. Scored against the shipped tables (dumped by tests/dump_weights.rs, not restated in Python): median 1.41x against a pre-registered 1.60x limit, worst-interior 2.02x against 2.20x. Recorded explicitly as an implementation check and NOT a predictive success, since the donor already scored 1.41x/2.02x on archived data before any code was written. Worst-overall 4.03x is the documented flat-extrapolation limit -- the DCT8x8 donor spans only f in [0.088, 0.875], so larger transforms' corner cells clamp rather than continuing to fall.

SCREEN: PREDICTION CONFIRMED, CONTRACT B STILL FAILS. Across 28 exactly-matched-rate cells, pooled butteraugli is better in 17 of 28 (mean -0.17%) and SSIMULACRA2 in 18 of 28 (mean +1.37) -- the first weight on this track to be net-positive on both. The pre-registered prediction holds: the 2 bpp arm halved from Phase 6.3's +13.10% mean to +6.74%, exactly as the improvement in high-frequency pricing (CSF 0.41x of target, donor 0.65x) predicted. But 11 of 28 cells regress on butteraugli, so promotion fails and production stays Flat.

READING THE 2 BPP MEAN HONESTLY. Its two regressors, s2/2 (+30.7%) and s5/2 (+24.7%), both sit at already-excellent absolute quality (butteraugli 1.6885 and 1.1264, so +0.52 and +0.28 absolute), and the 2 bpp MEDIAN is -0.03% -- the mean is an outlier effect, not a broad regression. That is a caveat in the donor's favour and must not be used to wave the failure away: a +30.7% relative regression on a scene the encoder was handling well is still a real regression.

THE RATE STRUCTURE IS THE FINDING. The donor is a large win at 0.5 bpp (SSIMULACRA2 better on every scene by +3.45 to +5.97, butteraugli 5 of 7 with a best of -12.3%), a clear win at 1 bpp (SSIMULACRA2 7 of 7), neutral at 2 bpp, and very nearly a no-op at 4 bpp (most cells within 0.1% butteraugli). That gradient is mechanistically consistent: the weight matters most where the fewest coefficients survive quantization, because that is where the cover decision changes what is kept; at 4 bpp almost nothing is zeroed, so pricing barely changes what is emitted.

WHERE THIS POINTS. Three phases now agree: 6.2b re-priced the transform-size axis (null), 6.3 re-priced frequency (rate-split), 6.5 re-priced frequency better (fades to nothing as rate rises). All three are bounded by HfQuantizer::choose picking the nearest reconstruction level rather than an RD-optimal one, so cover and CfL are the only decisions any weight can move. The next round belongs on the quantizer.

A rate-conditioned policy is the obvious next screen and the obvious trap: the donor is strongly positive below 1 bpp and inert above 2, so switching on rate would likely pass a corpus gate -- but 'helps at low rate' is a description, not a mechanism, and Phase 5 is full of content-dependent switches that did not survive. If screened, the mechanism (how many coefficients survive quantization) should be measured directly rather than proxied by the rate request.

One unexploited finding: Ahumada-Peterson's oblique-effect term r + (1-r)cos^2(theta), r = 0.7, correlates with the Phase 6.2 data at +0.475 radius-controlled over 1322 cells -- diagonals ARE less sensitive -- but the effect is not constant, running 1.11-1.39 at f = 0.10-0.25 (diagonals more sensitive) and 0.49-0.68 at f = 0.55-0.70. AP's constant r is wrong in both directions and the literature does not supply a frequency-dependent form. Deliberately kept out of this screen so the donor's contribution stayed isolated.

Full tables, the model comparison and the donor-choice matrix: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-quant-donor-frequency-weight.md. Raw rows, driver and checker: .agent/scratch/phase6-5-quant-donor-2026-08-12/.

### Peak-memory convention: JPXL sits between cjxl e7 and cjxl e9, and below e9 at 12 MP

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.encoder-memory-convention-2026-08-31/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`

Peak RSS measured per child through os.wait4 (not the cumulative RUSAGE_CHILDREN high-water mark), all encoders pinned to the same six physical P-cores at six threads, on the two locked anchors. At 12 MP (4000x3000): cjxl -e 7 -d 1.0 uses 365 MiB (32 bytes/pixel) in 0.86 s and -d 1.5 uses 353 MiB; JPXL Balanced q85 uses 1978 MiB (173 B/px) in 2.38 s; JPXL Balanced q85 with the E1-a retention raised to 24 MP uses 2404 MiB (210 B/px) in 1.97 s; cjxl -e 9 -d 1.0 uses 3227 MiB (282 B/px) in 16.05 s. At 4.3 MP: cjxl -e 7 252-253 MiB (61-62 B/px), JPXL 923 MiB (225 B/px, unaffected by E1-a because 4.32 M pixels never crossed even the old 8 MP threshold), cjxl -e 9 1198 MiB (292 B/px) in 5.59 s. There is therefore no single library convention to compare against, only a tier: against libjxl's comparable-speed single-pass tier (e7) JPXL uses about 5.4x the memory at 12 MP, while against its high-effort tier JPXL uses less than libjxl does (2404 MiB versus 3227 MiB with E1-a engaged, and 1978 MiB without) at roughly one eighth the wall time. libjxl's own footprint spans an order of magnitude across its effort range (32 to 282 B/px at 12 MP), which is the relevant context for the quality path's cost: JPXL's profile resembles a searching encoder because it is one, running several probe encodes plus a full decode-side render and metric evaluation per probe. Note the per-pixel figure is not flat -- JPXL is 225 B/px at 4.3 MP against 173 B/px at 12 MP -- so a fixed overhead dominates smaller frames, and the E1-a band between 8 and 24 MP now runs near 210 B/px, putting a 24 MP source close to 5 GB.

### Census raw-event replay is byte-identical but wall-slower with a 11-14 MiB memory cost; reverted

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.event-replay-negative-2026-09-01/1`

On the working tree atop 45d948630dec1bac11bc98e6a9ea727e33c2e2a8 plus the retained trailing-truncation change, retaining compact (pre-context, raw value) census events and replaying them into the token-tape recorder at exact pricing was byte-identical across the full 32-encode matrix (two anchors, quality/rate, t1/t4, default/scalar; large-anchor hashes matched the canonical 2d8e948e and 222358b8). Two independent 12-repetition pinned ABBA matched-rate screens against the truncation-only binaries showed the replay is slower, not faster, on the anchor where its ceiling was largest: 12 MP t4 1.0297 CI [1.0139,1.0454] and 1.0243 CI [1.0038,1.0524]; 12 MP t6 1.0243 CI [1.0131,1.0463] and 1.0164 CI [0.9982,1.0415]; the 4.3 MP cells straddled 1.0 in both runs. Peak RSS rose 11-14 MiB (4.3 MP) and 13-14 MiB (12 MP), confirming the transient raw-event tape cost. The eliminated second coefficient/context walk evidently reads data still cache-warm from the census, while the retained tape adds a multi-MiB cold store that is written during the census and re-read during replay. Both runs carried large clock drift (-68.3% and again), so paired intervals, not absolute walls, carry the verdict. The candidate was reverted per the retain-only-if-beneficial rule; the reverted tree rebuilt to binaries bit-identical (md5) to the retained truncation-only binaries.

### Exact sample-domain special transforms regress quality: honest negative, research mode removed

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.exact-sample-specials-honest-negative-2026-08-12/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/write.rs"`

WHAT WAS BUILT THEN REMOVED. SpecialTransformMode::ExactSampleDistortion re-opened Phase 5O's same-8x8 specials (Hornuss, DCT2x2, DCT4x4, DCT8x4/4x8, AFV0-3) at hierarchical leaves, scoring each with exact inverse-transform sample SSE after HF quantization plus an 8-bit DctSelect transition proxy. CLI --special-transforms exact-sample. Writer gate permanently widened to accept that vocabulary (Phase 5O wire evidence); large/rectangular families stay refused.

DISTORTION PROOF (kept). exact_sample_distortion_is_not_parseval_for_hornuss shows Hornuss's Parseval map (coeff SSE * 64) is not equal to inverse-recon sample SSE, so any scorer that reuses the square-DCT coefficient currency on specials is known-wrong.

SCREEN, 8 discriminating cells (5O winners and regressors), matched-rate against post-7.2 production. Butteraugli better in 1 of 8 (small1/2, -7.2%, still -5.8 SSIMULACRA2). SSIMULACRA2 better in 0 of 8, mean damage large (e.g. small4/1 -26.9 SSIM, +35.9% BA). Under ssimulacra2-primary and Contract B the gate fails. Full matrix not run.

DECISION. No operating point. Exact sample-domain distortion is the right currency for specials but not a sufficient selector under the current rate proxy and DctSelect charge. Research mode removed; production stays square hierarchical cover. Wire support for same-8x8 specials remains for a later scorer.

### Frequency weighting drives the cover objective where transform size did not, but a detection CSF is the wrong curve and fails its pre-registered check

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.frequency-is-the-live-lever-csf-is-the-wrong-curve-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/csf.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`

Phase 6.3 gave block_cost_bounded's Y distortion term a per-cell weight from the Mannos-Sakrison contrast-sensitivity function at 60 pixels per degree -- the conventional one-pixel-per-arcminute viewing assumption -- as A(f)^2, normalised to mean 1 over the non-LLF cells so HfQuantizers::lambda stays calibrated and only the distribution across frequency moves. CoverFrequencyWeight::Flat builds no table and cell_weight returns exactly 1.0, so production is bit-identical; the flat encode of test-set/20240501_110934 at 1 bpp still reproduces the Phase 5O row exactly.

AGREEMENT CHECK -- FAIL, PRE-REGISTERED. Tolerance (worst bin ratio <= 1.35x, Pearson r >= 0.80), the 60 ppd assumption and the 2p = 0.8924 conversion were all fixed before any number was computed, and nothing was adjusted afterwards. Result: worst bin ratio 3.14x, r = +0.408. Two distinct disagreements. Mannos-Sakrison attenuates towards DC (bin 0 predicted 0.830) where the measurement makes the lowest non-LLF frequencies the most sensitive (1.915) -- the known divergence between a detection CSF, which describes seeing a grating on a blank field, and distortion visibility on a masked natural image where low-frequency error appears as banding. And it rolls off far too hard at high frequency: top bin predicted 0.335 against 1.050 measured, where the measured curve rises and the model still falls.

SCREEN -- PROMOTION GATE FAILS, BUT THE MECHANISM IS LIVE. Across 14 exactly-matched-rate cells the overall count is 7 better / 7 worse on butteraugli, which conceals the structure. Split by rate it is unambiguous. At 1 bpp butteraugli improves in 5 of 7 (mean -2.20%, median -3.90%, best -16.4%) and SSIMULACRA2 improves in ALL 7 (mean +1.22, best +4.37). At 2 bpp butteraugli regresses in 5 of 7 (mean +13.10%, median +14.60%, worst +32.4%) and SSIMULACRA2 in 6 of 7. Two 2-bpp cells undershoot the cap by about 4.2%, inflating that mean by roughly a point without changing its direction.

THE CONTRAST WITH PHASE 6.2b IS THE POINT. 6.2b repriced the transform-size axis correctly and butteraugli moved by a mean of +2.03% with everything inside plus or minus 14%. The frequency axis moves it from -16.4% to +32.4% and moves SSIMULACRA2 by up to +4.37. Frequency is a lever that actually drives this objective; transform size is not. That is the durable finding, and it survives the CSF being the wrong curve.

WHY THE RATE SPLIT, AND WHAT THE WEIGHT SHOULD BE. The agreement failure predicts the screen exactly. The CSF under-weights high frequency by up to 3.14x. At 1 bpp most high-frequency coefficients quantize to zero however they are priced, so that error is inert and what survives is the model's correct instinct that low-frequency structure matters most. At 2 bpp those coefficients are coded and visible, and pricing them at a third of their cost makes the objective discard them. Measurement and screen therefore agree on the same correction: the weight must be far flatter at high frequency than a detection CSF, with no low-frequency dip -- which is exactly the shape Phases 6.0 and 6.2 measured and this model failed to reproduce.

PRODUCTION UNCHANGED. Flat stays the default. Both research controls (CoverSizePenalty, CoverFrequencyWeight) are retained, production-neutral and bit-identical, because the next candidate weight plugs into the same point.

WHAT COMES NEXT IS A DECISION, NOT A TWEAK. The obvious move is a weight with the measured shape, and that crosses the line the workspace manifest draws: a table fitted to butteraugli's response makes this project's perceptual model a derivative of libjxl's. It must be recorded as a decision before it is taken. Preference order: (1) a distortion-visibility model from open literature rather than a detection CSF, which keeps the same clean-room standing this phase had and which the screen has now characterised; (2) a two-parameter analytic shape whose parameters come from the encoder's own quantization geometry rather than from butteraugli, then checked against the measurement; (3) fitting the measured curve, explicitly recorded with its licence and provenance consequences.

One further note for whoever picks this up: the 1 bpp result is already a uniform SSIMULACRA2 win and a 5-of-7 butteraugli win. A rate-dependent weight is not principled as stated, but the split is evidence that the correct weight interacts with which coefficients survive quantization -- an effect no static table can capture, and a hint that the quantizer, still nearest-reconstruction rather than RD, is where the remaining deficit lives.

Full tables, the agreement matrix and the rate split: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-csf-frequency-weight.md. Raw rows, driver and checker: .agent/scratch/phase6-3-csf-weight-2026-08-12/.

### Instruction-mix profiling contradicts "no exact lever left": the top metric kernels are dominated by spill, shuffle and scalar FP

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.hot-kernel-instruction-mix-2026-08-31/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/src/restoration.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/src/**"`

perf record -F 997 --call-graph=dwarf -e cpu_core/cycles/ on a 12 MP Balanced q85 t8 encode at HEAD 70626bf (probes=3, prices=2, 9051 samples) reproduces the recorded leaf shares: horizontal_band_avx2 14.08%, epf_step_rows_fma 9.17%, vert_batch_avx2 7.77%, planes_to_positive_xyb_avx2 5.76%, accumulate_band_avx2 4.73%, choose_run_avx2 3.74%, vertical_strip_avx2 2.09%. Render plus metric is about 51% of the whole encode. Categorising each kernel's own samples by instruction class (perf annotate) shows the leaf-share reading that closed the E1 stream was incomplete. horizontal_band_avx2, the top leaf, spends only 9.6% of its cycles on vector work: 25.9% stack spill/fill, 21.9% shuffle/lane-transfer, 16.7% scalar-double FP (vaddsd/vmulsd/vcvtsd2ss), 12.9% scalar load/store, 13.0% scalar int/control. Two mechanisms are visible in the disassembly. First, blur::pole_step takes &[f64]/&mut [f64] slice parameters, erasing the statically known length 8 of step_lanes' state, so LLVM cannot keep prev/prev2/acc in registers across the three pole calls and spills every step. Second, blur::build_padded_lanes performs its 8-row lane interleave as eight strided scalar passes (body.iter_mut().skip(r).step_by(8)), emitted as vmovss %xmm0,(%r10,%rbx,8) and accounting for roughly 20% of the leaf. accumulate_band_avx2 shows the same shape (8.7% ymm against 30.8% scalar FP, 31.4% half-width xmm, 23.9% shuffle, plus a half-width vdivps). epf_step_rows_fma spends 35.6% on scalar int/control against 27.5% ymm, an indexing/bounds profile rather than a compute one. planes_to_positive_xyb_avx2 is properly 4-wide (61.4% ymm) but loses 16.1% to spills and 14.2% to shuffles, which qualifies the E1-e conclusion: the divider chain is throughput-bound, but a third of that kernel is not the divider. vert_batch_avx2 is the healthiest (62.4% ymm) with 21% still at half width on the f32 side. None of these are measured wall wins; they are codegen defects on kernels whose combined share is about 41% of wall, and each candidate fix is per-lane arithmetic-preserving and therefore gated by the existing byte-identity harness. The host is an i7-13700H with no AVX-512, so widening the f64 recursion beyond 4 lanes is not testable here.

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.jxl-oxide-previous-channel-properties-2026-08-17/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/modular_out.rs"`

Streams whose LF-group control-image MA tree splits on an H.4.1 previous-channel property (Table H.4 index 16 + 4j + 2, |rC - rG| of an earlier identical-shape channel, evaluated exactly as the clause's code: j from i-1 downwards over channels of identical width/height/shifts, rW = 0 at the left edge, rN and rNW falling back to rW) are decoded sample-exactly by jpxl-decode (tests/control_image_roundtrip.rs) and by djxl (the target-rate quality screen was measured through djxl decodes), but jxl-oxide 0.12.6 rejects every such stream with 'frame error: vardct error: modular stream error: entropy decoder error: ANS stream verification failed'. ### Lambda×4 under trailing truncation is the first rate-aware quantizer operating point that improves SSIMULACRA2 while keeping butteraugli gain

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.lambda-x4-is-the-operating-point-2026-08-12/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`

WHAT WAS BUILT. EncodeRequest::lambda_scale (default 1.0) multiplies the derived lambda before the cover objective and the Phase 7.0/7.1 RD weights read it. CLI --lambda-scale. Non-positive or non-finite values fall back to 1.0. The unit scale is byte-identical to the pre-Phase-7.2 path.

SWEEP. Same 28-cell matched-rate protocol as Phases 7.0/7.1, trailing truncation on, scales 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 / 4.0 / 8.0 against a flat nearest baseline that sets the byte cap. Primary 1 bpp row; s7/0.5 reported separately.

RESULTS, pooled. Scale 0.5: SSIM 1/28 mean -2.98, BA 14/28 mean +1.54% (worse). Scale 1.0 (Phase 7.1): SSIM 3/28 mean -0.68, BA 19/28 mean -3.46%. Scale 2.0: SSIM 15/28 mean +1.10, BA 23/28 mean -4.94%. Scale 4.0: SSIM 24/28 mean +1.94, BA 23/28 mean -6.81%, both better 22/28. Scale 8.0: SSIM 21/28 mean +2.21, BA 17/28 mean -3.06% (BA weakens at 4 bpp, +6.46% mean, undershoot -6.99%).

PRIMARY 1 bpp at scale 4.0: SSIM 7/7 mean +1.42, BA 7/7 mean -9.06%, both 7/7. Byte deltas at scale 4.0 by rate: -0.73 / -0.55 / -0.60 / -1.93%; the 1 bpp row is clean. s7/0.5 at scale 4.0: SSIM +6.79, BA -6.51% -- no longer an adverse outlier.

DECISION. An operating point exists. lambda_scale=4.0 under trailing truncation is the chosen point: first rate-aware setting that is non-regressing on SSIMULACRA2 and keeps (enlarges) the butteraugli gain. Scale 2.0 also clears the mean gate but is weaker; scale 8.0 loses BA at high rate. Promoted on EncodeRequest::for_target only; fixed-quantizer defaults stay nearest at unit lambda.

DIRECTION. In this encoder's R + lambda D form, higher lambda values distortion more and truncates less. The unit-scale arms over-zeroed for SSIMULACRA2 because the uniform-quantizer derivation under-weighted sample-domain distortion relative to what SSIMULACRA2 accounts as structure. Multiplying by four is an empirical correction, not a new derivation.

Full tables: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-lambda-calibration.md. Raw rows: .agent/scratch/phase7-2-lambda-2026-08-12/.

### Head-to-head vs cjxl 0.13: jpxl is at cjxl -e1 density, 5-24x slower, and its effort ladder is inert above level 1

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.libjxl-headsup-modular-2026-08-10/1`

Head-to-head against the libjxl oracle on the three-image real-photo corpus (.agent/scratch/realworld-bench-20260806T072202Z), lossless modular, both codecs at their default thread counts, on this Windows host. jpxl at effort 1/3/5/7/9 versus cjxl v0.13.0 (196a43d9, MinGW, AVX2) at -d 0 -e 1..9. Bytes and wall milliseconds:

small_0p8MP (1024x768): jpxl e1 1,075,465 @ 295ms; e3/e5/e7 identical bytes @ 649/837/1320ms; e9 1,037,868 @ 10,291ms. cjxl e1 1,082,673 @ 61ms; e3 890,029 @ 44ms; e7 873,503 @ 144ms; e9 866,855 @ 597ms.

mid_4MP (2400x1800): jpxl e1 5,157,974 @ 521ms; e3/e5/e7 identical @ 2258/3320/5680ms; e9 4,942,547 @ 55,156ms. cjxl e1 5,414,251 @ 33ms; e3 4,273,458 @ 139ms; e7 4,097,956 @ 520ms; e9 4,054,479 @ 2301ms.

large_12MP (4000x3000): jpxl e1 through e9 ALL emit 9,795,599 bytes, at 1272/6118/9774/18,200/65,437ms. cjxl e1 9,870,951 @ 54ms; e5 7,646,073 @ 632ms; e7 6,921,886 @ 1147ms; e9 6,756,132 @ 6825ms.

Three things follow. (1) Density: jpxl sits at roughly cjxl -e1, beating it by 0.8-4.7% on bytes, and is 20-31% larger than cjxl -e7 (12MP: 9,795,599 vs 6,921,886, +41.5% bytes for the same 1.1-1.3s of wall time). (2) Speed: jpxl -e1 is 5x slower than cjxl -e1 at 0.8MP, 16x at 4MP, 24x at 12MP -- the gap widens with size, so it is throughput, not fixed overhead. (3) The effort ladder is nearly inert: at 12MP levels 1 through 9 emit byte-identical output for 51x the wall time, and at the smaller sizes only level 9 moves at all (-3.5% / -4.2%) at 35x / 106x the time of level 1.

The mechanism behind (3) is visible in the code, not just the numbers: plan_for caps the tree at 2 leaves / depth 1 whenever the frame exceeds deep_search_sample_cap, whose largest value is 1<<18 = 262,144 samples at effort 9. Every image in this corpus, including the smallest at 786,432 samples, exceeds that cap, so no level ever searches a tree deeper than one binary split. The density levers the higher band would need -- many-context MA trees, RCT type selection (the encoder hardcodes YCoCg; H.6.3 defines 42 types), and LZ77 inside the cost model (already scoped as Phase 4D) -- are not reachable from the current ladder at any real image size.

How it was measured: a PowerShell driver (preserved at .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/headsup.ps1, raw output alongside it in headsup-2026-08-10.txt) times one encode per (image, codec, setting) with Diagnostics.Stopwatch around the process invocation and reads the output length from the file system. jpxl is invoked as `jpxl encode <ppm> <out> --effort N`; cjxl as `cjxl <ppm> <out> -d 0 -e N`, using the pinned Windows oracle build in JPXL/tools/oracle-bin (cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9, AVX2, per PINNED_REVISIONS.txt). Both codecs run at their own default thread count, so these are end-to-end wall times as a user would see them, not per-core algorithmic cost.

Scope limit: three photographs on one host, one timed run per cell, no warm-up. It is a direction-setting measurement, not a promoted baseline; the timings are not medians and should not be quoted as such.

### Historical lossy quality tables used asymmetric decoders

### Lossy RD on three metrics: 12-20% behind cjxl on SSIMULACRA2 but 39-53% on butteraugli, localising the deficit to perceptual bit allocation

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-perceptual-baseline-2026-08-10/1`

Rate/distortion baseline for the lossy VarDCT path against cjxl v0.13.0, scored on three metrics: PSNR (signal error), SSIMULACRA2 (perceptual, higher better, 100 = identical) and butteraugli distance (perceptual, LOWER better, and the metric cjxl -d actually optimises). Corpus: the three real photographs in .agent/scratch/realworld-bench-20260806T072202Z. JPXL swept by --bpp, cjxl by -d, cjxl output decoded with the oracle's own djxl. Full 24-cell table in .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/headsup-lossy-perceptual-baseline.txt.

THE HEADLINE: the size of the gap depends on which metric you ask, by a factor of three, and the two readings say different things.

Comparing at EQUAL QUALITY (interpolating cjxl's curve to jpxl's operating point), cjxl's bitrate saving is:

SSIMULACRA2 -- 0.8 MP ~17% (jpxl 80.0 at 1.988 bpp vs cjxl ~1.66), 4 MP ~12% (jpxl 85.3 at 1.996 vs cjxl ~1.76), 12 MP ~20% (jpxl 87.9 at 1.673 vs cjxl ~1.34).
PSNR -- 0.8 MP ~26%, 4 MP ~25%, 12 MP ~37%.
Butteraugli -- 0.8 MP ~43% (jpxl 3.56 at 1.988 bpp vs cjxl ~1.13), 4 MP ~39% (jpxl 2.01 at 1.996 vs cjxl ~1.21), 12 MP ~53% (jpxl 1.96 at 1.673 vs cjxl ~0.79).

Two conclusions follow, and they are not the same conclusion.

(1) On SSIMULACRA2 the codec is within 12-20% of cjxl. That is a much smaller deficit than the PSNR-only reading in jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-vardct-headsup-2026-08-10 suggested, and it says the transform, quantization and entropy layers are fundamentally sound -- this is not an encoder that is broadly behind.

(2) On butteraugli the deficit is 39-53%, three to four times the SSIMULACRA2 figure. Butteraugli is what cjxl tunes for, so some of that is expected; but a gap that much larger on one perceptual metric than another localises the deficit to PERCEPTUAL BIT ALLOCATION -- where bits go within a frame -- rather than to coding efficiency, which both metrics would punish equally. Concretely that points at the adaptive-quantization field (jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs), whose three constants (AQ_STRENGTH 0.25, AQ_CLAMP 1.0, CHROMA_AQ_WEIGHT 0.35) came from the 8-bit x265-family literature and had never been validated against any perceptual metric on this codec's output, because until this session the repository had none.

Speed, unchanged from the earlier PSNR-only run and still the largest practical gap: jpxl is 58-530x slower at every size and rate (8.7-71 s vs 0.09-0.20 s at 0.8 MP; 63-687 s vs 0.75-1.62 s at 12 MP).

Scope limit: three photographs, one host, one timed run per cell. The equal-quality bitrates are interpolated between adjacent cjxl rungs, not measured directly, so treat them as approximate. Direction-setting, not a promoted baseline. PSNR and SSIMULACRA2 and butteraugli disagree here by design -- do not quote one of them as "the" gap.

### Lossy VarDCT vs cjxl (PSNR-only, superseded as a summary): 58-530x slower; high-rate miss traced to LF-fill ordering at adjacent rungs

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-vardct-headsup-2026-08-10/3`

First rate/distortion comparison of the lossy VarDCT path against the oracle. Corpus: the three real photographs in .agent/scratch/realworld-bench-20260806T072202Z. JPXL swept by --bpp, cjxl v0.13.0 swept by -d, cjxl output decoded with the oracle's own djxl so a JPXL decode bug cannot masquerade as a cjxl quality difference. Raw original rows: .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/headsup-lossy-2026-08-10.txt.

SCOPE CORRECTION (revision 2, retained): this record measured PSNR only. jpegxl-rs.observation.lossy-perceptual-baseline-2026-08-10 re-measures SSIMULACRA2 and butteraugli and finds a 12-20% gap on one and 39-53% on the other. The original density result is only the PSNR gap.

Measured original (bpp, PSNR dB, encode ms): 0.8 MP -- jpxl (0.499,24.94,8724) (0.995,28.72,17602) (1.988,34.04,34973) (3.999,41.56,55646); cjxl (0.839,30.55,154) (1.466,34.22,94) (2.321,37.91,106) (3.428,41.00,104). 4 MP -- jpxl (0.498,27.47,38076) (0.995,32.64,55376) (1.996,37.40,106791) (3.645,41.62,178646); cjxl (0.565,32.27,551) (0.941,35.15,336) (1.490,37.78,341) (2.366,40.18,309). 12 MP -- jpxl (0.499,31.67,63214) (0.997,36.67,144969) (1.673,39.32,472352) (3.942,45.72,462885); cjxl (0.414,34.83,1534) (0.677,37.18,944) (1.074,39.54,897) (1.765,42.18,754).

(1) On PSNR, cjxl reaches equal PSNR at roughly 25-37% fewer bits. Superseded as a general quality summary by the perceptual record above. (2) Speed: jpxl was 58-530x slower because a targeted encode prices 15-40 full-frame plans; this remains the largest practical gap.

(3) HIGH-RATE UNDERSHOOT -- CAUSE CORRECTED AGAIN IN REVISION 3. Revision 1 incorrectly called it a ladder ceiling. Revision 2 correctly rejected that but then inferred from `24 fast` that bracketing/bisection exhausted the Fast cap. Phase 4M's new phase/rung telemetry shows that inference was also wrong.

At 0.8 MP / 4 bpp, the 20 Fast prices split into 3 Bracket + 7 Bisect + 2 Fill + 8 LF-fill; Fast best/upper were adjacent rungs 73728/73729 and Full started/ended at 73728. At 4 MP / 4 bpp, 24 Fast split into 3 Bracket + 14 Bisect + 3 Fill + 4 LF-fill; Fast best/upper were adjacent 73729/73730 and Full started/ended at 73729. The ladder had settled; the aggregate count included secondary LF probes.

The actual narrow defect was LF-fill order. With requested quant_lf=16 and only four remaining slots, absolute-distance order tried 12, 8, 24, 32. The first two make LF coarser while trying to spend an undershoot. Finer-only order reached 24, 32, 48, 64; exact pricing selected 64 and raised the 4 MP result from 1,954,100 to 2,003,736 bytes, reducing the miss from about 9.5% to 7.2%, for about a 2% single-run diagnostic wall increase. Lower-rate 0.8 MP outputs stayed byte-identical. Raw Phase 4M summary: .agent/scratch/phase4m-lf-fill-direction-2026-08-11.md.

The remaining 4 MP miss is not attributed here beyond the measured trace; the 12 MP / 2 bpp case has not yet been re-run with phase telemetry and remains unknown. Do not restore either the ladder-ceiling or generic Fast-bracketing-exhaustion diagnosis.

### The measuring host is a thermally-constrained hybrid laptop part; unpinned wall A/Bs cannot resolve the 1-3% effects several reverts were decided on

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.measuring-host-cannot-resolve-small-effects-2026-08-31/2` · scope `path "JPXL/tools/**"`

The measurement host is a 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13700H: 6 P-cores exposed as cpu0-11 with SMT (4.8-5.0 GHz) and 8 E-cores as cpu12-19 (3.7 GHz), no AVX-512, scaling governor powersave, turbo enabled, 24 MiB L3. Three consequences for every wall measurement recorded on this host. First, there is no clean 8-thread operating point: the standing t8 anchor necessarily places workers on E-cores or SMT siblings, whose throughput differs from a P-core by roughly 40%, and which worker lands where varies run to run. Second, the part is thermally constrained, so a schedule that runs one arm's repetitions before the other charges the entire thermal drift to the second arm; the package was observed at 97 C with the pinned P-cores clocked at 2485 MHz against a 4800 MHz maximum, and clock drift of +26.8% was recorded across a single short measurement block. Third, harnesses in this tree read getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss after each child, which is a cumulative high-water mark across every child ever reaped and therefore reports the largest run so far rather than that run; wall_e1g.py compounds this by taking a running max of it, so its per-arm RSS columns cannot distinguish the arms. JPXL/tools/quiet_ab.py was written to address these: it pins to the 6 physical P-cores with SMT siblings excluded, interleaves arms in palindromic ABBA order so linear drift cancels within a repetition, takes per-child rusage through os.wait4, reports a percentile-bootstrap 95% confidence interval on the paired ratio, and refuses to run above load 0.7 or alongside a live cargo/rustc/jpxl. A null A/B of the release binary against a byte-identical copy of itself, run deliberately on a loaded 97 C host, returned ratio 1.0111 with CI [0.9179, 1.0470] at 5 repetitions: a plus or minus 5% noise floor from a pair of arms that are the same program. Any verdict on this host at an effect size inside that band, taken without pinning and interleaving, measured the host rather than the change. @jpegxl-rs.evidence.e1e-two-chain-xyb-negative-2026-08-30 (+0.8-1.4%, loaded host) falls inside it.

### Retiring the tree-depth cap changes nothing; the cheap ranker's unit mismatch was the inertness

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.modular-depth-is-not-the-lever-2026-08-10/1`

MA-tree depth is not what the modular effort ladder was missing. The cheap ranker's unit mismatch was.

The deep_search_sample_cap was believed to be the blocker: it collapses the tree to max_leaves=2, max_depth=1 whenever a frame exceeds it, and its largest value (1<<18) is below every real photograph, so no effort level ever searched past one binary split. Retiring it changes nothing. With `--modular-deep-cap full` on the 4 MP corpus image, efforts 7, 8 and 9 all converge on the SAME output -- 4,942,547 bytes, fingerprint 771811b28ce7ab6e -- as they do with the cap in place. Depth beyond one split, and the finer THRESH_FINE grid that efforts 8-9 add, buy exactly zero bytes. The greedy split loop stops improving after its first round regardless of how much depth it is allowed.

What was actually wrong is a units error in lossless::total_cost_source: it added an unscaled whole-frame `ma_tree_bit_cost * sections` to a residual estimate covering only 1/row_stride of the frame. A split's saving was therefore divided by the stride while its cost was not, over-pricing every extra context by exactly the sampling ratio -- and the ratio grows with frame size, which is why the ladder looked progressively more inert on bigger images. Measured proof of the mechanism before the fix, on the 4 MP image: at stride 1 (effort 9) the winning split IS found (4,942,547 B); at stride 4 (effort 7) the same split is rejected (5,157,974 B). Same content, same candidate, different verdict purely from the sampling ratio.

With estimate_residual_bits_sampled extrapolating to whole-frame bits, effort 7 finds at stride 4 the tree that previously only stride 1 could reach: 0.8 MP 1,075,465 -> 1,037,868 B (-3.5%), 4 MP 5,157,974 -> 4,942,547 B (-4.2%), 12 MP unchanged at 9,795,599 B (no split wins there at any stride, before or after). Against cjxl -e7 the 4 MP gap narrows from +25.9% to +20.6% -- real, and nowhere near closed.

Two consequences worth acting on. (1) Effort 7's output is no longer byte-identical to the pre-effort-ramp encoder; that anchor property was retired deliberately and the corpus gate now pins the default (effort 1), which short-circuits the search entirely and is untouched. (2) Effort 7's wall time at 4 MP rose from ~5.7 s to ~47-50 s for the same ~71 residual scans, because the tree that now wins contains the Weighted (H.5) predictor, and estimate_residual_bits_sampled must fall back to a full sequential scan for any Weighted-containing tree -- so once Weighted wins the sweep, every one of the 56 split candidates carrying it forward becomes a full-frame scan. Bounding that is the obvious next target: score split TOPOLOGY with a stateless proxy and restore Weighted only in per-leaf refinement.

Scope limit: three photographs, one host, single runs. Direction-setting, not a promoted baseline.

### One frequency curve prices all three squares, quantizer normalisation does not, and the objective under-penalises large transforms by 4-21%

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.one-frequency-curve-fits-all-squares-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/tests/perceptual_frequency.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`

Phases 6.0 and 6.1 measured DCT8x8 alone. block_cost_bounded's entire job is comparing one large square against four sub-quadrants, so Phase 6.2 measured DCT8x8, DCT16x16 and DCT32x32 on an identical DCT32x32-aligned crop, each with its own I.7.3 inverse, its own I.2.5 default matrix and its own LLF exclusion. Y channel, two photographs, two amplitudes, 5,292 probes per sweep. Two harness corrections were required: amplitude is now in sample-domain units (I.7.2's inverse scales a square's amplitude by side, which idct_2d_raw carries and the harness divides back out), and amplitude is scaled by side/8 so total injected sample-domain energy is equal across sizes -- which makes raw butteraugli directly comparable between them.

RESULT A -- THE PERCEPTUAL WEIGHT IS SIZE-INDEPENDENT. Binned by radial normalised frequency and levelled to each size's own f=0.4-0.5 bin, the equal-coefficient-error curves agree to a worst shared-bin disagreement of 1.15x, with six of nine shared bins within 5%. A single weight expressed as a function of normalised spatial frequency prices all three square transforms. This is what the phase was scoped to test and it passes.

RESULT B -- LARGE TRANSFORMS ARE UNDER-PENALISED. Because total injected energy is equalised, the raw per-bin means compare directly, and they are not equal: the same total squared sample error costs 4% to 21% more butteraugli when carried by a DCT32x32 basis than by DCT8x8 bases -- monotonically in size, in every one of nine bins, on both photographs (e.g. low frequency 3.837 / 4.338 / 4.655). Error on a 32x32 support is spatially coherent over a large region, where the same energy spread across sixteen independently-signed 8x8 patches is closer to noise and easier to mask. block_cost_bounded assumes the opposite -- that its to_sample_domain = side^2 factor makes candidates of different sizes comparable. It does not, so the hierarchical cover is biased toward merging. The correction is a per-transform scalar, not a per-cell table.

RESULT C -- QUANTIZER NORMALISATION IS REJECTED AS THE FORM OF THE WEIGHT. The step-proportional residual, which Phase 6.1 proposed to ship as sum (delta_k / step_k)^2, does not collapse across sizes: worst shared-bin disagreement 2.05x, and the shapes differ qualitatively. DCT8x8's residual is 6.1's shallow bowl (1.21 -> 0.83 -> 1.23); DCT32x32 rises monotonically from 0.59 to 2.79. The cause is in the matrices: the I.2.5 defaults' non-LLF Y step ratio is 2.86x at DCT8x8 but 8.05x at DCT16x16 and 13.05x at DCT32x32, so they coarsen high frequencies far more aggressively at large sizes than perception justifies. Weighting by 1/step^2 uniformly would be approximately right for DCT8x8 and badly wrong for DCT32x32 -- it would price high-frequency error in a 32x32 block as cheap exactly where measurement says it is the most expensive thing in the table. That is the new bias this phase existed to catch, caught before it shipped.

REPLACEMENT PLAN. Result A licenses a single first-principles contrast-sensitivity curve evaluated on each transform's own normalised grid, checked against the measured curve rather than fitted to it, plus Result B's per-transform level correction. Both are cheap -- a per-cell constant and a per-transform scalar, precomputed once -- and this form is MORE clean-room-defensible than 6.1's proposal, because it stops borrowing its shape from the dequant tables. jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase6-3-quantizer-normalised-y-distortion is superseded accordingly.

CONVENTION ERROR FOUND AND DISPOSITIONED. idct2d_8x8 (used by 6.0/6.1) and idct_2d_raw (I.7.3, the encoder's own convention via forward_dct_rc -> dct_2d_in_place, and the layout HfQuantizer indexes its matrix in) are both orthonormal but differ by a transpose of the coefficient index. Nothing moves: the I.2.5 default square matrices were measured exactly symmetric (worst relative asymmetry 0.000000 for every channel at all three sizes), so 6.1 paired every cell with the correct step regardless, and 6.0's spread and stability statistics are invariant under relabeling. Only the u/v labels in the published 6.0/6.1 tables are transposed relative to the encoder's grid, and the measured Y map is near-symmetric anyway.

STILL NOT ESTABLISHED. Y only, and cover/CfL only, since HfQuantizer::choose remains nearest-reconstruction. Result B's direction is consistent across every bin and both images but its magnitude should be re-measured at the rates the corpus actually encodes at before being used as a calibration constant. The f=0.4-0.5 reference bin is a normalisation choice rather than a fitted parameter, and it is also a local rise against its neighbours -- the same index-4 feature 6.0 and 6.1 both flagged as probably belonging to butteraugli's multi-scale pyramid; that it survives at all three sizes is weak evidence it is a property of the metric, and another reason to fit a smooth CSF rather than these numbers.

Full tables and method: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-per-transform-frequency-weight.md. Raw output: .agent/scratch/phase6-2-per-transform-2026-08-12/.

### jxl-oxide 0.12.6 narrows LfQuant at the signed-16-bit boundary

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.phase5-aqoff-jxloxide-incompatibility-2026-08-11/3` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/rate.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/tests/vardct_oracle.rs"`

The two failures originally attributed to HfMul are caused by optional LF fill producing otherwise-valid signed-32-bit G.2.2 LfQuant samples that jxl-oxide 0.12.6 narrows at the signed-16-bit boundary. A fixed-input black-box sweep agrees through quant_lf 78 (LF peak 32669, decoder peak 1) and fails at quant_lf 79 (LF peak 33088, decoder peak 255/RMSE 71.28); fixed HfMul values 1 through 65 remain decoder-consistent. Part 1 D.3 permits 32-bit Modular samples when modular_16bit_buffers is false, G.2.2 carries LfQuant through Modular, and djxl plus jpxl-decode agree, so this is an external-decoder defect rather than a JPXL wire error. The fixed-quantizer API retains the standard's full signed-32-bit range. Target-rate LF fill now declines only candidates whose planned LfQuant exceeds signed 16-bit, preserving compatibility without weakening the oracle gate. All 10 VarDCT oracle tests pass afterward.

### Active EPF remains production; special transforms need a better selector

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.phase5-quality-policy-screen-2026-08-11/11` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/src/main.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/rate.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/tests/rate_loop.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/tests/vardct_oracle.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/ids.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/plan.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/write.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/tests/vardct_plan.rs"`, `path "test-set/**"`

Phase 5G promoted AQ Off, quant_lf 8, and no LF-fill after improving Butteraugli in all twelve six-scene cells by 7.6% to 34.2%. Phase 5H showed lower global quant_lf is content-dependent. Phase 5I promoted one active EPF step with uniform Sharpness 7 after it improved Butteraugli, RMSE, and Butteraugli pnorm3 in all twelve cells; the target-rate default remains byte-identical to that screened candidate. Phase 5J tested two-pass HF reconstruction-error AQ and removed it after mixed results. Phase 5K tested deeper EPF and removed it after three Butteraugli regressions and broad SSIMULACRA2 loss. Phase 5L retained checked X/B quant-matrix scale signalling but kept neutral X2/B2 after global alternatives were inconsistent. Phase 5M rejected median-source-variance spatial EPF after eleven of twelve polarity cells regressed Butteraugli and all regressed SSIMULACRA2. Phase 5N rejected a finer integer-HfMul AQ representation after both polarities regressed Butteraugli in all eight direction cells. Phase 5O proved that the existing clean-room core and generic writer can emit the same-footprint Hornuss, DCT2x2, DCT4x4, DCT8x4/DCT4x8, and AFV families. Optimistic local selection improved Butteraugli in eight of twelve cells by up to 15.0%, but regressed four by up to 6.2% and reduced the number of within-20% cjxl anchors from two to one. A realistic global DctSelect transition charge preserved a high-rate gain but did not remove two discriminating low-rate regressions. All temporary Phase 5O surfaces were removed at the requested stopping point and the production fingerprint restored. Production remains within 20% of equal-rate cjxl effort-7 on only small3/1 and mid2/2; the other ten anchors remain 23.8% to 78.1% worse. The most promising measured continuation is special-transform selection with a reconstruction/perceptual or exact map-cost signal, not another global activity threshold or scalar penalty. Raw tables are in .agent/scratch/phase5g-corpus-summary-2026-08-11.md through .agent/scratch/phase5o-special8-2026-08-11.md.

### Parallelizing the serial varblock render and linearization cut 12 MP quality wall 21%; ratio 3.11x -> 2.46x on the measuring host

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.pqc-large-frame-render-parallel-2026-08-25/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quality.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/src/evaluator.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-plan-render/**"`

Per-probe phase attribution on the locked 12 MP anchor (fast-debug, comparing 1-thread vs 8-thread walls to identify serial stages) showed the reference side of SSIMULACRA2 already precomputed once per search (PrecomputedReference with ReferenceRetention::Moments at <=24 MP); the serial per-probe stages were varblock reconstruction (500-730 ms; a 12 MP frame is one LF group, so group-level parallelism contributed nothing) and transfer-curve linearization (105-180 ms). After banding both over the EncodeExecutor (map_ordered varblock chunks of 2048 with serial disjoint scatter; banded LUT lookup), varblocks measure ~235 ms and linearize ~18 ms; per-probe render+metric fell ~1.3 s to ~0.77 s. Release wall on the anchor at 8 threads: 4.923 s -> 3.906 s (-21%), matched-rate ratio 3.11x -> 2.46x on this host (the recorded 6.31x/8.02x baselines were another host/state; the relative move is the reliable signal). Byte-identical streams on six image/target cells, identical canonical scores, cross-thread determinism at threads 1/4/8 in both profiles, peak working set unchanged at 1,899 MB, all touched-crate gates green. Remaining per-probe residual is co-dominated by the still-serial varblock sample scatter (~part of 235 ms) and the already-parallel metric (~380 ms); the largest further headroom is score-changing (navigate on a reduced pyramid or downscaled reconstruction, full-resolution only for final verification), which requires a Contract B promotion A/B.
