### Perceptual encodes of 50 MP sources reach ~12 GB RSS; two concurrent measurement runs OOM-killed a 31 GB host twice

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.pqc-memory-50mp-oom-2026-08-22/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quality.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`, `path "JPXL/tools/codec_compare.py"`

The kernel OOM-killed jpxl twice on 2026-08-22 (12:54 anon-rss 9.9 GB; 13:28 anon-rss 11.9 GB) while two agents measured the perceptual controller concurrently on a 31 GB host without swap, taking the Claude Code session down both times. Both kills were perceptual encodes of photo-large-20260606_150624.ppm, an 8160x6120 (50 MP) locked-holdout source; three of the thirteen holdout images are that size. Peak RSS on the quality path scales at about 240 bytes per pixel (2.9 GB at 12 MP per pqc-pr4b-memory-12mp), so a 50 MP encode needs about 12 GB and cannot share the host with a release build or a second such encode. Measurement runs must serialise large encodes and cap each process with ulimit -v so a runaway fails instead of killing the session; the reduction itself (tiled scorer, plan lifetimes) remains the PR 4b follow-up.

### The one-shot falsification screen fails on corpus coverage, not on the design: transform features halve the error, the tail is two under-represented classes

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.pqc-one-shot-gate-fails-on-corpus-coverage-2026-08-24/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/**"`, `path "JPXL/tools/**"`

On the expanded 56-image / 38-family corpus with production-endpoint oracle labels (fresh Balanced pixel plans over the complete effective ladder; zero censored rows even at target 95, so the old predictor's 81-94% high-target saturation was an artifact of its HfMul=1 ladder cap), the memo's pre-PR5 falsification screen fails: best leave-one-family-out median |ln(predicted/oracle crossing)| is 0.220 with p90 0.805 (bounds: quick p90<=0.45; production median<=0.10, p90<=0.30). Three findings shape the path forward. (1) Transform-domain features materially help, as the memo predicted: source-only p90 1.28 vs source+transform 0.81, median 0.42 vs 0.22, first-or-one-correction success 1.00. (2) The failure is class coverage, not model form: photo, photo-scene, text-screenshot, noise-lowlight, line-art and grayscale classes sit at held-out p90 0.36-0.67 (near or past the quick bound), while saturated (p90 3.58) and sky-noise gradient (p90 4.07) dominate the tail - both effectively class-held-out because their families carry near-unique content. (3) The fallback discipline works: with honest intervals the simulated controller routes 99% of requests to the exact path, keeping bytes at 1.0016x but eliminating the wall win (expected reconstructions 3.98 vs the current median 4). Per the memo, production controller work stops here until the corpus grows (>=25 independent families per critical class; saturated and banding-stress content first); the PR5 mechanism exists behind the off-by-default `one-shot-controller` cargo feature and remains inert without a gate-passing model.

### Quiet-host wall anchors: 12 MP 5.42x (4t) / 4.25x (8t); the quality path's fixed costs alone sit near 2x, so the 2.0x target is unreachable by search improvements

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.pqc-wall-quiet-host-attribution-2026-08-25/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quality.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/src/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-plan-render/src/**"`

Interleaved matched-score timing (wall_current.py recipe: one warm-up per kind, 10-run schedule, 5 GiB address-space cap, host state per run) on a quiet host with the current release binary: 4.3 MP anchor quality/rate 2.021/0.521 s = 3.88x at 4 threads and 1.824/0.566 s = 3.22x at 8; 12 MP anchor 5.464/1.007 s = 5.42x at 4 threads and 3.988/0.938 s = 4.25x at 8. The 4-thread rate median (1.007 s) reproduces the 2026-08-23 baseline exactly, so the comparable quiet-host series at 12 MP/4t is 8.00x (2026-08-23) -> 5.42x (after the one-shot promotion cut probes 5->3); the 2.46x recorded on 2026-08-25 divided by an inflated ~1.59 s rate denominator measured under load and is not comparable. Phase attribution (12 MP, 8 threads): plan 366 ms, render_metric 1985 ms (three pixel probes at 642-697 ms each), entropy 79 ms, emit 99 ms, two exact prices 89 ms each; ~1.4 s of the 3.99 s wall is outside the controller (source PPM load, metric reference precompute, feature extraction, output IO). Consequence: the quality path's fixed costs excluding all scored probes (~1.83 s at 8 threads) are already 1.95x the rate path, and a perfect single-probe controller would land near 2.7x, so the wall-anchors 2.0x acceptance cannot be met by search improvements alone; it requires reducing per-pixel render+metric cost ~2-3x (score-identity risk) or renegotiating the target. Separately, the band-parallel varblock scatter is exact but wall-neutral at the 12 MP anchor: render_metric 2043/2168 ms (pre-change binary) vs 2107/2057 ms (post), and the 4 MP varblock stage is 45 ms at 4 threads in both trees, so the earlier ~50-100 ms/probe scatter estimate was high. Raw runs, traces, and comparisons are in the kept scratch entry pqc-scatter-20260825 (wall-scatter.json, trace-*.jsonl).

### Per-probe attribution: reused-probe planning already collapses; metric then render dominate each probe

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.probe-attribution-2026-09-01/1`

Advisory per-probe plan/render/metric fields added to PerceptualObservation and QualityProbe (trace-only; schema stays jpxl.quality-trace/2) attribute each canonical pixel probe on both locked anchors at t4 and t6. On the 12 MP anchor the fresh probe is plan 344 ms (the structural build) + render 293 + metric 413, while reused probes pay plan 30-123 + render 180-245 + metric 247-707; on 4.3 MP reused-probe planning is 13-50 ms. The plan share collapses on reused probes, so the structural anchor (cover/CfL capture plus the HfMul overlay) already removes nearly all per-probe planning, and render+metric are irreducibly per-candidate work: no exact structural simplification of measurable size remains in the probe sequence (the reference, evaluator scratch and forward-DCT sharing already exist and the exact-codegen closure on the render/metric kernels stands). ### One-shot stop rate is 4.3% and fully attributable to calibration; finalist non-monotonicity is 1/76

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.probe-contract-b-shadow-2026-09-01/1`

A zero-stream-change shadow corpus run (95 quality-guard fixtures, 94 scored - the 7x7 fixture is below the metric's 8x8 floor; quality 85 balanced, t4, one accumulated jpxl.quality-trace/2 JSONL) measures both Contract B levers. The true one-shot stop rate is 4/94 = 4.3%, exactly equal to the cells that are both confident (decision_path one_shot, 13 cells) and in-band (first probe feasible with overshoot <= 1.0 score point): the two gates fully explain the observed stops. The losses are calibration, not mechanism: 9 of 13 confident cells missed the band and 8 of 12 in-band cells were not confident; overshoot median is +1.14 points and predicted-rung/winner-rung median 1.34 (the upper quantile is systematically conservative). Baseline pixel probes per encode are {1:4, 2:12, 3:40, 4:8, 5:30}, mean about 3.5, with 81/94 cells on the fallback bracket path. Finalist non-monotonicity is 1/76 two-finalist cells (1.3%) - one 700x700 synthetic at adjacent rungs 10006/10150 where entropy training flipped the byte ordering (3635 vs 3617) - while elsewhere the coarsest feasible finalist is also the smaller stream (median 9.3% smaller). So skipping the second exact price buys nothing on ~99% of cells but for a 1.3% rare-byte-change tail, and raising the stop rate is a calibration question on the qpv2 upper quantile and confidence gates, not a new stop rule. Raw: .agent/scratch/exact-base-encoder-20260901/corpus-shadow.jsonl.

### Q3: the two-anchor controller's second anchor extrapolates with exponent 2 and overshoots on smooth photos, so Balanced falls back to the exhaustive controller above the ceiling (mid2 2 bpp 5.9 s vs 0.42 s at 1 bpp)

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.q3-balanced-second-anchor-overshoots-above-the-ceiling-2026-08-18/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/rate.rs"`

second_anchor_rung places the second anchor at effective scale E1 * (target/bytes1)^2, i.e. it assumes bytes ~ E^0.5. Measured from the standing traces (first anchor E=32768, Balanced), the exponent p with E_final/E1 = (target/bytes1)^p is 1.57/1.71/1.78 on the mid photo at 0.5/1/2 bpp, 1.64/1.74/1.80 on the large photo and 0.95/0.95/1.05 on the smooth mid2 photo. On mid2 the second anchor therefore lands 3-4x too fine, the log-log finalist prediction from two anchors that far apart misses the tolerance band, and the search falls back to the exhaustive controller: 5,920 ms median (frozen Q1 binary 5,219 ms, undershooting) at 2 bpp against 423 ms at 1 bpp; the 2 bpp target is now reached (1,079,753 B). Below the ceiling nothing changed (mid 1 bpp Balanced 423 ms vs 428 ms for the frozen Q1 binary, alternating 4x3). A first-anchor-adaptive exponent (or a bracket check before trusting the second anchor) is the follow-up; it changes every Balanced/Fast rung choice and needs the full corpus gate. Raw traces: .agent/scratch/q3/timing-*.txt and the JPXL_RATE_TRACE dumps in the Phase Q3 section of JPXL/docs/optimize.md. Observed on the Phase Q3 commit d1005c4e.

### Q3: no variance-based per-block HfMul field or activity-adaptive EPF sharpness beats the frame-uniform quantizer, even on a sixteenth-octave lattice; the size penalty and X scale 3 stay negative on the corpus

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.q3-per-block-fields-lose-on-a-fine-lattice-2026-08-18/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`

The Phase 4J/5A 'AQ is a net loss' screens measured a lattice that rounded any coarsening to a full octave (baseline HfMul 2). Q3 rebuilt the field on baseline 16 (global_scale/16, quant_lf*16, mul in 8..=32) with a 3x3 minimum erosion (AqMode::FineMasking), its sign mirror (FineUniform), and a refine-only edge field that only touches atoms more than a dead zone above their quietest neighbour (EdgeRefine). On the mid photo at 1 bpp Balanced (control PSNR 35.38, SSIMULACRA2 77.18, Butteraugli 2.78 / 3-norm 0.872) every strength of every field lost SSIMULACRA2 and 3-norm: fine-masking 0.05 -0.19 / +1.7% (max-norm -7%), 0.10 -0.62 / +5.9%; fine-uniform 0.03 -0.55 / +3.1%; edge-refine 0.05 at contrast 6 -0.45 / +1.5%, at contrast 2 -2.6 / +6.8%. Each field costs 6-16 KB of mul plane (1-3% of the file) before any reallocation, and fine-masking moves 3-norm -3..-4% in the three quietest variance quintiles but +2%/+7% in the busiest two, which dominate the norm. The activity signal log2(1+65025*var) spans 0..13 on this photo, so even strength 0.05 moves most blocks. Activity-adaptive EPF sharpness (7 ramping to 0-3 on busy blocks) is worse everywhere (SSIMULACRA2 -0.5..-1.1, 3-norm +2.7..+8.5%): the Phase 5I uniform sharpness 7 is doing real work in busy content. On the standing corpus against a same-binary control, --cover-size-penalty measured is SSIMULACRA2 -0.037 (photos) / -0.134 (scenes) with 3-norm +0.67% / +0.42%; --x-qm-scale 3 is +0.021 / -0.007 with 3-norm +0.51% / +0.42%; both together -0.010 / -0.139. ### Q4: the writer spends 1.5-2.0x the cover proxy's residual bits with a stable DCT8 < DCT16 < DCT32 ordering; SSIMULACRA2 and Butteraugli diverge because JPXL's SSIMULACRA2-first policy accepts localised worst-case error that Butteraugli's max-norm and masking model punish

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.q4-rate-proxy-audit-and-metric-divergence-2026-08-18/3` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`

Rate audit (tests/rate_proxy_audit.rs, 1 bpp Balanced): actual/proxy including fixed bits is 1.63/1.37/1.27 (mid), 1.60/1.35/1.53 (large), 1.89/1.60/1.78 (mid2) for DCT8/16/32; per token, interior zeros cost 0.40-1.11 bits (falling with transform size), nonzero coefficients 3.3-4.1 bits against bitlen+1, non_zeros symbols 1.7-3.7 bits each; a DCT8x8 varblock walks 22-33 coefficient positions per three channels, a DCT16x16 94-173, a DCT32x32 70-389. Calibrated per-size scales are consistent across the three photos in ordering (residual under-pricing 1.56/1.63/1.88 mid, 1.52/1.58/1.76 large, 1.84/1.89/2.0 mid2). Metric divergence: at matched bytes JPXL leads cjxl -e7 on SSIMULACRA2 in 9/9 cells and trails on Butteraugli max-norm in 7/9 (up to +43%), 3-norm in 7/9 (up to +14%) and PSNR in 8/9 (up to 0.54 dB). SSIMULACRA2 averages multi-scale structural similarity over the frame and forgives localised error; Butteraugli reports a max-norm (and a high-power 3-norm) of a masking-based difference map, so one visible patch next to flat content sets the score; PSNR is mean-square error. JPXL's target-rate policy was promoted SSIMULACRA2-first (quant_lf 4, quant-donor frequency weight, trailing truncation at lambda x4, uniform EPF 7, hierarchical merges), each improving average structure while trading MSE and accepting occasional localised errors at edge/flat DCT8x8 blocks (Q3 localisation), and cjxl targets Butteraugli distance directly; the two encoders sit at different points of one tradeoff surface. Q4's rate calibration is the first change since Q1 that improves SSIMULACRA2 (+0.048 photos / +0.059 scenes) and Butteraugli 3-norm (-0.15% / -0.13%) together; the per-block allocation levers of Q3 did not. Observed on the Phase Q4 commit 547da94d.

### The standard's own quant matrices carry a third of the frequency weighting; measuring distortion in quantizer-normalised units cuts Y mispricing 2.65x to 1.86x

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.quantizer-normalised-distortion-is-the-lever-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-conformance/tests/perceptual_frequency.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quantize.rs"`

Phase 6.0 injected equal coefficient error per DCT8x8 cell and measured a 2.65x Y-channel perceptual spread. Real quantization never injects equal coefficient error: it injects error proportional to each cell's step, and HfQuantizer builds that step as scale[channel] * matrix.at(x, y) from the I.2.5 default dequant matrices, which are themselves perceptually shaped. So 2.65x was an upper bound on the decision-relevant mispricing.

Phase 6.1 re-ran the identical sweep -- same crops, corpus, amplitude ladder, per-block signs, zero-self-distance assertion and sample-domain SSE control -- with the injected amplitude at each cell scaled by that cell's default DCT8x8 step, RMS-normalised over the 63 non-LLF cells so total injected energy matches 6.0 exactly and the two experiments sit at the same operating point. scale[channel] is constant across cells, so it cancels under that normalisation and the matrix is the step shape.

RESULT. Normalised butteraugli spread, mean map over 6 runs (2 photographs x 3 amplitudes), with the weakest pairwise stability of those runs: Y 2.65x (r 0.961) becomes 1.86x (r 0.843); X 2.35x becomes 6.76x; B 1.56x becomes 11.60x. Per-run and without averaging, every one of the six Y runs is flatter under step-proportional injection than its 6.0 counterpart (2.49/2.72/2.92/2.63/2.72/3.00 becomes 2.43/2.07/1.83/2.21/1.90/1.80). Y's step shape rises with frequency by 2.86x while 6.0's weight falls by 2.65x, so the matrices compensate in the right direction and remove about 36% of the log-domain mispricing.

WHAT THIS LICENSES. The current objective measures D_flat = sum_k delta_k^2 in dequantized coefficient units. The obvious first-principles alternative, using only data the encoder already builds, is quantizer-normalised distortion D_qn = sum_k (delta_k / step_k)^2. D_qn equals the true perceptual cost exactly when w0[k] * step_k^2 is constant, which is precisely what 6.1 measures, so the measured residual IS the mispricing that would remain after the switch. Switching cuts Y frequency mispricing from 2.65x to 1.86x for one precomputed per-cell multiply in the scoring loop and no change to the quantizer.

Three properties make this the cleanest lever measured on this track. (1) First-principles, not fitted: the weight comes from the standard's own matrices; butteraugli only checks the direction and size of the improvement rather than supplying numbers, which is the distinction the workspace manifest's clean-room note draws and the opposite of fitting a table to 6.0's response. (2) Unit correctness, not tuning: HfQuantizer::step's own doc says it exists so callers can price distortion in the same units choose quantizes in, and the scorer does not do that -- there is an argument for the change that needs no perceptual measurement at all, and 6.1 only prices it. (3) Sharp scope: Y only.

RESIDUAL SHAPE. The Y residual (mean over 6 runs, stdev 0.052) is a shallow bowl, not 6.0's monotone fall: the defaults slightly over-coarsen the extreme corner (1.33-1.36 along v=7 and u=7) and slightly under-coarsen the band at index 4 (0.73-0.80). The index-4 feature is the same one 6.0 flagged as probably belonging to butteraugli's multi-scale pyramid rather than to vision, so it is not a target.

CHROMA IS DEFERRED, NOT JUDGED. X and B fail the gate and the direction is probably real -- 6.0 showed B's response is nearly flat per unit coefficient error, so shaping injected error by a 20.67x step ratio must produce an uneven perceptual cost -- but the magnitudes are contaminated. At a 20.67x shape and amplitude 1.0x the channel standard deviation, the highest-frequency B injections are far outside any operating point the encoder reaches and butteraugli's max-norm saturates. The amplitude ladder was designed for a constant shape and does not control realized distortion when the shape spans an order of magnitude. Do not apply quantizer normalisation to chroma until a re-run chooses amplitude per cell to hold realized butteraugli in a fixed band.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, unchanged from 6.0. This moves cover and CfL selection only, because HfQuantizer::choose is nearest-reconstruction rather than RD. It is DCT8x8 only, and the cover decision's whole job is comparing transform sizes, so wiring an 8x8-only weight into block_cost_bounded would introduce a new bias rather than remove the old one -- Phase 6.2 blocks the encoder change. And a 1.86x residual remains: this is an improvement to the ruler, not a correct ruler.

### Selective truncation cuts the SSIMULACRA2 damage by 62% but still regresses 25 of 28 cells: the remaining term is lambda, never calibrated against any perceptual metric

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.selectivity-halves-the-damage-but-lambda-is-the-remaining-term-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quantize.rs"`

WHAT WAS BUILT. HfQuantizer::truncate_trailing is a block-level backward pass: quantize greedily, then walk back from the last nonzero pricing each trailing-nonzero drop at its own token bits plus the interior zeros it exposes times ZERO_TOKEN_BITS, against weight[cell] * (target^2 - (recon - target)^2), accepting while favourable. It only ever removes from the end, so unlike Phase 7.0's per-coefficient rule it cannot strip texture uniformly. Y is truncated before d_y_hf is read, so chroma CfL decorrelates against the Y the decoder will actually reconstruct. ZERO_TOKEN_BITS = 1.0 is a stated conservative estimate, not a measurement: token counts are exact but token bits depend on an ANS cluster the census builds after the walk.

PROVED AGAINST THE REAL WALK, not a restatement. On a 256x256 fixture at 1 bpp the pass removes 11.8% of nonzero tokens but collapses 42.6% of zero tokens (total symbols 20,098 to 13,529), with the non_zeros symbol count unchanged. That asymmetry is the signature: a magnitude rule would move both counts together, a mid-run rule would raise the zero count.

SCREEN, 28 cells on the Phase 7.0 protocol. Pooled SSIMULACRA2 better in 3 of 28 (mean -0.68); butteraugli better in 19 of 28 (mean -3.46%). Against Phase 7.0 on the identical protocol (SSIMULACRA2 4/28, mean -1.80; butteraugli 20/28, mean -5.21%): selectivity cut the SSIMULACRA2 damage by 62% while keeping most of the butteraugli gain.

SO THE DESIGN HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED AND THE GATE STILL FAILS. Restricting removals to those that actually truncate a walk did exactly what Phase 7.1a predicted. But under the SSIMULACRA2-primary decision the metric regresses in 25 of 28 cells, so production stays QuantizerChoiceMode::Nearest.

WHY THIS POINTS AT LAMBDA, SPECIFICALLY. The finding is sharper than 'rate-aware quantization hurts'. A pass that removes ONLY coefficients whose removal collapses a run -- the most rate-efficient removals available anywhere in the block -- still costs SSIMULACRA2 on 25 of 28 cells. The problem is therefore not WHICH coefficients are dropped; it is that dropping ANY HF coefficient at this operating point costs more structure than the bits are worth on SSIMULACRA2's accounting. That is a statement about the exchange rate.

lambda is derived in HfQuantizers::new_with_scales as 16 / mean(s^2) over the non-LLF DCT8x8 cells, from a uniform-quantizer argument: halving a step costs one bit per coefficient and moves s^2/12 to s^2/48. It has NEVER been calibrated against a perceptual metric. If it over-values bits, every rate-aware decision over-zeroes regardless of selectivity -- which is exactly the pattern across 7.0 and 7.1. Note that ZERO_TOKEN_BITS and lambda are the same knob in effect, both scaling rate against distortion, so sweeping the former is not an independent experiment; calibrating lambda is.

CAVEATS. The high-rate byte undershoot recurs, milder than 7.0's: byte deltas by rate are -1.38 / -0.36 / -2.00 / -3.98%, so the 1 bpp row is clean and carries the clearest signal (butteraugli better on 6 of 7 by a mean of -8.00%, SSIMULACRA2 worse on 6 of 7) while the high-rate rows are partly confounded. s7/0.5 is an outlier that should not be read as a normal cell: its flat baseline SSIMULACRA2 is already negative (-10.08, the scene is destroyed at that rate) and it lands 7.00% under cap; its -5.17 delta dominates the 0.5 bpp mean, which is -0.25 without it rather than -0.95. The within-block pass ignores cross-block context coupling, and the natural-order vector is allocated per varblock -- acceptable for an opt-in mode, would need hoisting before any promotion.

Full tables and the walk-verified proof: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-trailing-truncation.md. Raw rows and driver: .agent/scratch/phase7-1-truncation-2026-08-12/.

### The reference SSIMULACRA2 implementations' f32 recursive Gaussian leaves a ripple that inflates near-lossless scores' error on flat content, growing with image size; the in-tree metric runs the recursion in f64

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.ssimulacra2-f32-recursion-ripple-2026-08-22/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`

The Charalampidis truncated-cosine Gaussian used by SSIMULACRA2 is generated by three resonators with poles on the unit circle (feedback 2cos(omega_k) and -1), so in f32 every rounding error persists as an undamped ripple of a few 1e-6 along each row and column. The metric's edge maps rectify that ripple (max(0, .)), which raises the measured error wherever the image is nearly flat. Measured against the rust-av ssimulacra2 0.5.1 crate with the in-tree f64 recursion: synthetic flat-heavy content at score ~93 scores +0.14 above the crate at 256x192, +0.35 at 333x257, +0.73 at 640x480 and +1.07 at 1024x768, while a photograph at score ~82 differs by only 0.03 (0.27 MP), 0.09 (1.1 MP) and 0.18 (4.3 MP); at scores below 90 synthetic pairs agree within 0.13 and photographs within 0.03. With the recursion in f32 (no FMA) the in-tree metric instead scored below the crate by the same pattern. The blur itself matches the crate to 1.5e-5 (f32) or 6e-6 (f64) per sample. Decision: the in-tree metric keeps the f64 recursion (closer to the defined filter, host-independent) and its parity test pins a size-scaled tolerance (0.05 + 0.5*sqrt(MP) below score 90, 0.1 + 1.6*sqrt(MP) above; photographs 0.1 + 0.1*sqrt(MP)).

**derived_from** `@jpegxl-rs.policy.perceptual-metric-clean-room/1`

### A rate-aware quantizer moves quality an order of magnitude more than any cover lever, but its crude rate proxy over-zeroes: butteraugli 20/28 better, SSIMULACRA2 4/28

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.the-quantizer-is-the-lever-and-its-rate-proxy-is-the-defect-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quantize.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`

HfQuantizer::choose now optionally minimises residual_bits(q) + rd * (recon - target)^2 instead of the nearest |recon - target|, where rd is exactly the coefficient block_cost_bounded already multiplies squared coefficient error by (lambda[channel] * side^2 * size_penalty * frequency_weight[cell]). Minimising that per coefficient minimises the same total the cover search sums, so the quantizer and the cover finally agree on one currency. The table is installed on the quantizer after lambda is calibrated; None is the shipped nearest rule and keeps that path bit-identical. The zero shortcut is skipped under RD (it would bypass the wider zeroing the mode exists for) and the SIMD choose_lane4 delegates to four scalar choose calls under RD so the two stay bit-identical by construction. cell_lower_bound's provable prune assumes the nearest rule, so s8-cover-prune is not validated against this mode.

RESULT: THE BIGGEST LEVER ON THE TRACK, AND A SHARP METRIC SPLIT. Across 28 cells on the Phase 6.2b/6.3/6.5 corpus and protocol, butteraugli improves in 20 of 28 (mean -5.21%, best cell -29.9%) while SSIMULACRA2 improves in only 4 of 28 (mean -1.80). For scale on the identical protocol, Phase 6.2b moved butteraugli +2.03% with everything inside plus or minus 14% and Phase 6.5 moved it -0.17%. By rate: 0.5 bpp butteraugli 5/7 (mean -2.08%) SSIMULACRA2 4/7 (-0.72); 1 bpp butteraugli 5/7 (mean -8.79%) SSIMULACRA2 0/7 (-3.00); 2 bpp butteraugli 4/7 (-4.29%) SSIMULACRA2 0/7 (-2.36); 4 bpp butteraugli 6/7 (-5.66%) SSIMULACRA2 0/7 (-1.10).

THE SPLIT IS REAL, NOT A RATE ARTIFACT. At 0.5 and 1 bpp the byte deltas are -0.34% and -0.43%, properly matched. At 1 bpp butteraugli improves by a mean of -8.79% while SSIMULACRA2 regresses on EVERY scene by a mean of -3.00. The mechanism is over-smoothing: widening the dead zone removes small nonzero coefficients, butteraugli's max-norm rewards the reduced peak error, and SSIMULACRA2 penalises the lost texture. A rate proxy that cannot see zero runs zeroes uniformly rather than selectively, so it takes texture everywhere instead of where runs would actually pay.

SECOND, SEPARATE FINDING: RD WORSENS THE HIGH-RATE UNDERSHOOT. At 2 and 4 bpp the RD arm lands 3.0% and 5.7% under the cap on average, worst -7.8%, on the same cells whose nearest encode already undershot (the known Phase 4M behaviour). A smaller stream at every quantizer setting pushes the rate loop further from a cap it already struggled to reach. Those two rate rows are therefore confounded and must not be read as matched-rate comparisons -- though the 4 bpp butteraugli improvement is achieved while spending 5.7% FEWER bytes, which is a genuine rate-distortion improvement on that axis.

CONTRACT B FAILS on material SSIMULACRA2 loss (0 of 7 scenes better at 1, 2 and 4 bpp); production stays QuantizerChoiceMode::Nearest.

WHERE THIS POINTS, AND WHY IT IS SHARPER THAN A NULL. The work record pre-registered that a null would mean the deficit is not in per-coefficient decisions and the track should turn to the entropy model. It was not a null -- the quantizer moved quality an order of magnitude more than any cover-side lever -- and it STILL points at the entropy model, for a better reason: the rate term works and its PROXY is what is wrong. residual_bits charges magnitude bit length plus sign and, as sources/outside-advice.md states, knows nothing about entropy context, zero-run behaviour, coefficient order, neighbouring nonzeros, token probabilities or table overhead. The classic rate-distortion quantization win is zeroing to extend a zero run, and this proxy cannot see runs at all. A run- and context-aware rate estimate would zero selectively, keeping the texture SSIMULACRA2 measures and the coefficients that extend no run. entropy.rs already tokenises with the exact C.2.3 hybrid-uint arithmetic the writer uses, so that replacement has a foundation, and re-running this exact screen against it is the cleanest possible A/B with everything else held fixed.

Two process notes. Any future mode that changes stream size at fixed quantizer settings must report achieved-versus-requested bpp as a first-class number: the undershoot regression here was not anticipated by the protocol and would have silently confounded a weaker result. And butteraugli and SSIMULACRA2 disagreeing this sharply and this consistently (20/28 against 4/28) is information about the metrics as much as the encoder -- Phase 5 promoted on butteraugli with SSIMULACRA2 as a guard, and if a lever can move them in opposite directions this reliably, that promotion rule needs restating before the next promotion rather than after.

Full tables and the confound arithmetic: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-rate-distortion-quantizer.md. Raw rows and driver: .agent/scratch/phase7-0-rd-quantizer-2026-08-12/.

### residual_bits prices only a fifth to a half of the emitted symbols, and the lever it misses is walk truncation, not magnitude

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.the-rate-proxy-is-blind-to-most-symbols-and-the-lever-is-truncation-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/walk.rs"`

WHAT THE WALK CHARGES (18181-1 I.4, read from crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/walk.rs). Per varblock and channel: one non_zeros symbol in a neighbour-predicted context; then a coefficient token for EVERY order position from num_blocks up to and including the last nonzero, interior zeros included; then it stops, so positions after the last nonzero cost nothing.

residual_bits(q) charges 0 for a zero and bit_length(|q|) + 1 otherwise, so it is wrong three ways: interior zeros are free to it but cost real tokens; the non_zeros symbol is invisible; and truncation is invisible.

MEASURED, driving the real walk_frame rather than a reimplementation, on test-set/20240501_110934 at the promoted target-rate policy. Share of emitted symbols residual_bits prices: 21.7% at 0.5 bpp, 33.7% at 1 bpp, 50.9% at 2 bpp -- so it is blind to 78.3%, 66.3% and 49.1%. Zero-valued coefficient tokens, real symbols charged nothing, are 73.1% / 62.9% / 45.8% of all coefficient tokens. Totals emitted: 110,650 / 291,954 / 500,106 symbols.

THE LEVER IS TRUNCATION, NOT MAGNITUDE. Zeros sitting immediately before each block's last nonzero number 0.91 / 1.56 / 1.43 per varblock-channel. So zeroing one block's last nonzero frees its own token PLUS about 1.56 more at 1 bpp -- roughly 2.6 symbols -- while zeroing a coefficient in the middle of a dense run frees nothing at all. residual_bits credits a flat ~2 bits for both. That indifference is the whole Phase 7.0 failure in one sentence: given two coefficients of equal magnitude the proxy cannot prefer the one whose removal collapses a run, so it zeroed by magnitude alone and stripped texture uniformly, which is exactly what SSIMULACRA2 penalised in 24 of 28 cells.

THE BLINDNESS SCALES THE WAY THE DAMAGE DID. The invisible share is highest at low rate (78.3% at 0.5 bpp) and falls as rate rises (49.1% at 2 bpp), because sparse blocks are mostly zeros. Phase 6.5's donor weight helped most at low rate and faded to nothing by 4 bpp; Phase 7.0 did most of its damage where blocks are sparse. Both are consistent with rate structure mattering most where the proxy sees least.

WHAT THIS FORCES ON THE DESIGN. Because the last-nonzero position is a property of the whole block, a per-coefficient rule is structurally incapable of this selectivity WHATEVER its lambda -- Phase 7.0 could not have worked as constructed. Phase 7.1 must therefore be a block-level backward pass: quantize greedily, then walk back from the last nonzero deciding which trailing nonzeros to drop, pricing each drop at its true saving (its own token plus the interior zeros it exposes) against its true distortion. That is the classic last-position rate-distortion decision, and this measurement says it is the high-value piece rather than one option among several.

NOT ESTABLISHED. Token counts are exact here; token BITS are not -- each symbol's real cost depends on its ANS cluster and hybrid-uint configuration, which the census builds after the walk, so a count-based estimate remains a proxy and the record should keep saying so. The contexts also couple across blocks, since a block's non_zeros feeds the neighbour prediction grid for later blocks, and a within-block backward pass ignores that. One image, three rates, one policy: the proportions will move with content, the structural facts will not.

Full tables and method: JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-08-12-rate-proxy-gap.md. Raw output: .agent/scratch/phase7-1a-rate-proxy-gap-2026-08-12/.

### Correctly repricing the cover's transform-size axis does not improve quality: the extra splits cost more bits than the better size choice buys

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.transform-size-axis-is-not-the-deficit-2026-08-12/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/src/main.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`

Phase 6.2 Result B measured that block_cost_bounded's side^2 sample-domain normalisation does not make candidates of different sizes comparable: at equal injected sample-domain error a DCT32x32 basis costs 4-21% more butteraugli than DCT8x8 bases. Phase 6.2b screened that correction alone, split out of Phase 6.3 because it is one scalar per size rather than a CSF derivation, and because it answers the prior question 6.3 depends on -- does re-pricing the cover objective move Butteraugli at all.

CONSTANTS. Butteraugli is not linear in injected energy, so the measured excess cannot be used as a distortion multiplier directly. Over the measured 4x energy step it follows ba ~ E^p with p = 0.4477, 0.4477 and 0.4433 for the three sizes (mean 0.4462), a consistency that makes the conversion trustworthy; a butteraugli ratio r means r^(1/p) of distortion, mapping the 3.8% and 5.7% mean excesses onto multipliers 1.0000 / 1.0881 / 1.1331 for DCT8x8 / DCT16x16 / DCT32x32, stable across both probe amplitudes.

RESULT -- HONEST NEGATIVE. Across 14 exactly-matched-rate cells (7 test-set photographs at 1 and 2 bpp; measured encoded to neutral's achieved byte count; both decoded with the pinned djxl) butteraugli improved in 5 cells and regressed in 9, mean +2.03%, median +1.18%, range -5.9% to +14.2%. SSIMULACRA2 regressed in 11 of 14, mean -0.41. Measured lands 0.55% under the cap on average -- the rate loop's undershoot, worth about +0.55% butteraugli on this corpus's local RD slope -- so roughly a quarter of the mean is that confound and about +1.5% is real. The confound cannot explain the +14.2% worst cell and does not touch the SSIMULACRA2 loss at all.

WHY A CORRECT MEASUREMENT PRODUCED A WORSE ENCODER. Result B is not wrong; it holds on two photographs, in every frequency bin, at both amplitudes. What fails is the inference that correcting it improves the encode. Charging large transforms more makes the cover split more -- on the mixed-detail unit fixture DCT16x16 falls from 10 to 5 and DCT8x8 rises from 24 to 44 -- and those splits cost DctSelect signalling and per-varblock overhead. At a fixed byte cap those bits come out of quality everywhere else, and the better size decision does not pay for them. The RD tradeoff near the current operating point is flat enough that a 9-13% repricing moves the decision without moving the outcome.

CONSEQUENCE. The cover's transform-size axis is not where the Butteraugli deficit lives. Result B is therefore NOT carried into Phase 6.3 as a promoted correction; 6.3 screens the Result A frequency weight alone. The CoverSizePenalty control is retained rather than removed -- production-neutral, exactly 1.0, bit-identical -- so 6.3 can test the combination cheaply.

This also weakens the prior for 6.3, which is worth stating before running it: one axis of this objective was repriced correctly and the perceptual result did not follow. The frequency axis is a much larger mispricing (2.65x against 1.09-1.13x) and applies within every candidate rather than only between sizes, so it is not the same experiment -- but a second null would strongly suggest the deficit is not in cover/CfL selection at all, and that the next round belongs on the quantizer, which is still nearest-reconstruction rather than RD.

### Two-probe corrected-stop replay: best variant 2.85 mean probes, floor held, bytes neutral in geo-mean; success is set by first-probe distance, not slope

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.observation.two-probe-corrected-stop-replay-2026-09-02/2`

An offline replay (JPXL/docs/experiments/2026-09-02-two-probe-corrected-stop-replay.md; script and per-cell output kept in .agent/scratch/two-probe-replay-20260902) ports the quantizer ladder and the canonical navigator core of quality.rs to Python, validates the port against the deployed q85 Balanced t4 trace corpus (85/91 probe sequences reproduced rung-for-rung, 89/91 probe counts; replay mean 3.484 against deployed 3.462), and simulates a deterministic two-probe path on the 91 fixtures with 2026-09-02 oracle curves: the deployed first probe, then one correction aimed at the crossing (aim 85.45) from the measured loss and a slope estimate, accepted when feasible inside the existing 1.0-point band, the unchanged navigator as fallback. No variant approaches the advisor target (mean <= 1.5, <= 2 probes on 90%): the best ungated variant (prior slope 0.9, in-band first probes trusted, one second correction) gives mean 2.846 on the corpus and 2.429 on the 63 non-saturated non-tiny cells, with 48.4% (60.3% in-domain) at two probes or fewer; a 0.5 move gate gives 3.011 (2.587 in-domain). Every variant leaves every cell with a feasible final rung. Byte geometric mean against the deployed finalist is 0.995-1.006, but the ungated variants carry a fallback tail to +30% and a fair overshoot against the oracle crossing of 1.168 (deployed 1.150), while 0.25-0.5 move gates bound the in-domain tail to +9% with overshoot 1.143-1.145. The corrected stop lands in band 23/29 times when the first probe is within 0.25 ln scale of the crossing, 7/23 in [0.25, 0.5), and 0/14 beyond 1.0; the oracle slope does not improve this (33 stops against 36 with the prior), and only 36.7% of non-in-band first probes are within 0.25 (median 0.32, p90 1.38). Probe-wall proxy from the trace's per-probe millis: 0.884 ungated, 0.937-0.940 gated (>= 4 MP cells 0.895 / 0.952). Oracle-curve interpolation error on the deployed probes is median 0.20 points but p90 6.92 in the saturated class, so counterfactuals inside that class (26 cells, deployed mean 4.12 probes) are not trustworthy at band resolution. The three OOD (log2_pixels) 12 MP photos start at the legacy rung 73727, +1.14..+1.40 ln above the crossing (flagged model median +0.51..+0.64), and spend five probes including the finalist rebuild.

### The perceptual closure stands, but three exact base-encoder candidates merit measurement

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.exact-base-encoder-frontier-2026-09-01/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quantize.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/vardct/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/src/encode/**"`

The 2026-08-31 exact-codegen closure remains the right conclusion for the perceptual render/metric kernels, and probe policy remains the only double-digit quality-wall lever. A fresh matched-rate profile nevertheless identifies a separate exact base-encoder sequence worth screening. First, replace truncate_trailing's per-varblock Vec of all nonzero positions with a backwards cursor that finds only last/previous positions and reports each dropped cell so Y reconstruction is updated without a whole-lane rescan. This is local, Contract A, and has a 4.99% inclusive rate-cycle / 1.55% quality-cycle ceiling. Second, retain an optional compact raw event tape during the entropy census and replay it after clustering/config training, avoiding the second coefficient-order/context walk; this is cross-crate and has a 5.48% rate ceiling plus about 25 MiB transient raw-event storage on the 12 MP anchor. Third, specialize the TokenTape ANS emission path around a once-validated inline slot lookup; this has a 3.99% rate ceiling and is lower priority because the realizable fraction may be small. Screen in that order, one change at a time, with byte identity across t1/t4 and SIMD on/off, then `quiet_ab.py` on both anchors; profile shares are not wall claims. Do not reopen blur transpose, 128-bit vertical f32, XYB regroup, EPF bounds removal, coarse-scale serial scheduling, or cross-stage colour fusion without a new profile: their expected values remain around the measurement floor or their arithmetic remains mandatory. Do not describe these base-encoder candidates as a substitute for the Contract B probe-count decision: even all three together are unlikely to equal one avoided 422-489 ms canonical probe.

### Handoff: the exact-codegen frontier on the quality path is closed; the only remaining lever of size is probe count, which needs a Contract B decision

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.exact-codegen-frontier-closed-2026-08-31/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/src/restoration.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`, `path "JPXL/tools/**"`

State at handoff. The 2026-08-31 round landed four byte-identical changes worth -5% at 4.3 MP and -11 to -13% at 12 MP against HEAD 70626bf, roughly three times the -4.4% the whole preceding E1 stream achieved: ROW_LANES 8 to 6 in the horizontal blur (register pressure - six live [f64; N] arrays needed twelve of AVX2's sixteen ymm at eight lanes and spilled every sample), the pooled fourth powers hoisted out of accumulate_band's ordered fold, E1-a reference retention re-adopted under the renegotiated memory budget, and EPF's reciprocal-sigma divide hoisted to once per 8x8 block. Wall anchors are now 2.27x and 3.17x at four threads against 3.0x and 4.5x ceilings, with the rate path statistically unchanged.

Why this frontier is closed. The round began because instruction-mix profiling contradicted the E1 closure's claim that no exact lever remained; that was correct, and the defects it exposed are now fixed. What is left is fine-grained tuning with expected effects at or under the measurement floor: the build_padded_lanes transpose (~2%, and made harder by this round, since a six-wide interleave does not map onto the 8x8 shuffle networks that make an AVX2 transpose cheap), vert_batch's f32 side still at 128-bit (~1%), planes_to_positive_xyb's spill and shuffle overhead (~1-1.5%, with no lane constant to sweep - it is a scalar zip LLVM autovectorises - and E1-e already failed there), and the four-row-per-band scalar remainder that ROW_LANES=6 introduces (~0.8%). Each needs a full measurement round against a harness floor of about 0.5%. The expected value per item no longer justifies the measurement cost.

Where the remaining size actually is. Render plus metric is about 51% of a Balanced encode: the controller runs roughly three probe encodes, each followed by a full decode-side render and a full SSIMULACRA2 evaluation, where libjxl runs one encode. Probe count is worth more than any remaining kernel. Every exact route to cutting it is closed with evidence - surrogate navigation three times (S1, S2, S3), exact-rung speculation at the pairability gate (B1, 1/1213), and the slope-prior skip (RT2, J2b). So the next real step is a deliberate search-policy change screened by the standing Contract B gate, which is an operator decision about accepting a different quality-risk profile, not a measurement anyone can settle by profiling.

Method note for whoever picks this up. Two of five hypotheses this round were wrong and both looked persuasive first: pole_step's slice parameters erasing the lane count (inline(always) had already exposed it) and EPF's per-access bounds checks (the 35% scalar int/control is loop control LLVM had handled). Both were caught by A/B rather than shipped on a plausible story. Within-symbol instruction shares rank codegen defects but cannot rank a change - when the bounds-check removal was measured, the int/control share moved the wrong way because the symbol's other work shrank. Use JPXL/tools/quiet_ab.py and believe the interval, not the point estimate.

### Modular full search is chaff on real content; the lean config should be the default

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.modular-effort-lean-default/1`

On real photographic and smooth content the full modular search earns zero bytes over a single-predictor, single-leaf, collapsed search, while costing ~16x the wall time. Measured at 12MP (jpxl bench modular --diag): effort 1 does 1 residual scan, effort 7 does 71, and both emit the identical fingerprint dc380915d983b360 / 9,795,599 bytes. A content sweep (.agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10) shows effort 1 within 0% of best on photos and gradients, ~3.7% on a flat-block screenshot, at 5-17x the speed.

Per the bpg-rs precedent (commit 4e68042 'effort-tier restructuring': three canonical presets with explicit pipeline policies, the expensive tier kept cheap where it does not help), the expensive machinery (Weighted full-scans, the 56-candidate split grid, per-leaf refinement, finer stride, palette/squeeze trials) should be demoted to opt-in rather than remaining a tax on the default path. It is deliberately NOT deleted: those methods are load-bearing on content the synthetic fixtures do not represent (real UI/line-art -> palette; textured/noisy -> Weighted), and proving a method universally dead needs a broader real-world corpus.

Prose citations (V-005: an assessment cannot target a work record via supported_by): the implementing work is jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4e-modular-effort-ramp; the measurement evidence is jpegxl-rs.evidence.modular-search-chaff-2026-08-10 and jpegxl-rs.evidence.modular-effort-ramp-landed-2026-08-10.

### N2's stateful LadderNavigator does not pay for itself once N0 and N1 have landed

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.n2-navigator-does-not-pay-for-itself/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/**"`

Read against the tree after N0 and N1 (see @jpegxl-rs.work.ladder-navigator-unification), the residual duplication N2 would remove is small and its reducers genuinely differ, while the cost is a restructuring of the two most parity-sensitive files in the crate.

What N0 and N1 already removed is the real duplication: one quantizer ladder, and one copy of the log-domain crossing mathematics. What is left in the two controllers is bookkeeping, and it is not the same bookkeeping.

1. The reducers are deliberately opposite. rate.rs keeps the largest feasible *byte count* ever priced, tie-broken toward the finer rung (rate.rs Search::eval), precisely so a non-monotone entropy pocket cannot lose a candidate already proved to fit. quality.rs keeps the *coarsest feasible rung* (Navigator::coarsest_feasible), because a perceptual candidate that meets the floor at a coarser quantizer is strictly better. A shared observation store cannot own either reducer.

2. The no-repeat caches differ in kind. rate.rs's is a lookup into the priced trace that returns the cached byte count so the caller can tighten a bracket without a second encode, and the trace itself is the hard budget counter. quality.rs's returns a bool and its counter is separate, because its store also carries retained ValidatedPixelPlan payloads under a two-finalist retention rule.

3. The step rules are structurally different, and the plan's next_action() loop cannot drive both without pushing the arithmetic back out to an adapter. The rate loop brackets by integer octaves of effective scale and bisects by false position with the fraction clamped into the bracket; the perceptual loop expands by a loss ratio raised to 1/alpha with a margin that compounds per attempt, then tightens at the crossing. Reproducing the perceptual expansion inside a generic navigator would have to recompute the ratio as exp(y_thr - y_from)^(1/alpha) instead of (loss_from/loss_thr)^(1/alpha) - mathematically equal, not bit-equal - which is exactly the parity drift the plan's own risk section names.

Subtracting all of that leaves roughly sixty lines of linear-scan bookkeeping to share, in exchange for restructuring rate.rs (2900 lines) and quality.rs (2650 lines) around a common observation type. The stated justification for sequencing N0-N2 first - that they make every subsequent speed feature single-implementation - is already discharged by N0 and N1 for the mathematics, which is the part every later phase actually reuses.

Consequence for the sequence: N3 (confidence-adaptive probe budgets) does not depend on N2. It needs predict_v2's interval, saturation_risk and ood_flags routed into QualityBudget, which is entirely inside quality.rs, and R1 (RenderScratch) is independent of both. The Authority and NavigationPrior types N2 was to introduce are worth keeping as a design commitment for S1, but they belong where S1 puts them, not in a navigator with no other consumer.

### Paired candidate lanes cannot speculate the next rung exactly; B1 is closed

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.paired-candidate-lanes-cannot-speculate-exactly/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/quality.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`

B1 (paired-candidate evaluation, CandidateLanes<2>) is closed at its pairability gate. The quality navigation chooses rungs on a dense integer scale ladder as a deterministic function of the previous probe's exact score; without that score, the best in-process replay of the navigator's own decision core guesses the next rung exactly 1 time in 1213 across 644 corpus cells (gate h >= 0.7). The guesses are often close (tighten probes median 1.8-2.8% relative scale error; the probe-1 expansion is unguessable at median 33%), but B1's exactness contract discards a mis-speculated lane, so closeness pays nothing. The only pairing that could work - probing the speculated rung instead of the aim - is a Contract-B policy change that moves finalists, the same cost class the RT2 J2b gate closed. The frequency premise (97.4% multi-probe encodes) was never the constraint; determinism-without-the-score is.

### Correction: the '118x' figure is a wall-time ratio, not a density gap; jpxl-modular already beats cjxl -e1 on bytes

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-density-gap-is-vs-e7-only/1`

jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-order-correction (this session, prior revision) and the original jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped scoping both read the source claim '~118x slower than cjxl e1 for essentially identical output size' as evidence of a density/model-strength gap, and used that to justify front-loading 4A (Weighted predictor) and 4C (global tree) -- both density levers -- ahead of 4B (sampled property-gather, a search-time lever). The 4.0b density + decode-validity gate (jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4-0b-density-gate-2026-08-08, real corpus, current binary, decode-validated through both jpxl-decode and djxl) shows this reading was wrong: '118x slower... for essentially identical output size' means exactly what it says -- 118x is a TIME ratio (confirmed: 37.97s jpxl vs 0.317s cjxl -e1 at 12MP = 120x), and 'essentially identical output size' is accurate, not a euphemism for 'much larger.' Measured size ratios: jpxl-modular is 5-8% SMALLER than cjxl -e1 at every size class (0.944/0.953/0.992 across 0.8/4/12MP). There is no density gap versus cjxl -e1 -- jpxl already wins there. The real density gap is versus cjxl -e7 (max-effort search) only: jpxl trails by 16-42%, growing with image size (1.157/1.259/1.415).

This reverses the priority ordering. Modular's dominant, unambiguous problem is wall-clock cost (100-120x), driven by the 67 full-plane cheap-tier residual scans per plan_for call (lossless.rs:154-248) that 4B (sampled property-gather) directly targets. The density gap that does exist (vs e7 only, not e1) is smaller in relative terms (16-42% vs 100-120x) and is what 4A (Weighted predictor) and 4C (global tree) would address. Corrected sub-phase order: 4.0 (done) -> 4.0b (done) -> 4B -> 4A -> 4C -> 4D (optional tail, per the earlier not-on-hot-path finding which still holds).

4B remains the higher-implementation-risk item (proving sampled winner-selection matches full-scan selection, the 'invasive piece' per the original scoping) but is now also the higher-payoff item, reversing the earlier trade-off that ranked 4A/4C first partly because they looked cheaper AND more impactful. 4A is still cheap to build (mirrors jpxl-decode/src/modular/weighted.rs) and can run opportunistically alongside 4B design work if convenient, but should not block 4B on the critical path.

### Advisor correction: Phase 4 order is 4.0b density-gate -> 4A -> 4C -> 4B -> 4D(optional), not 4A+4D-first

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4-order-correction/1`

An independent Opus advisor review of jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped, run against live code (not the prior scoping summary), verified all four cited code facts (PREDICTOR_CANDIDATES omits Weighted at lossless.rs:70-78; use_global_tree hardcoded false at modular/mod.rs:1094; full-plane cheap scans at lossless.rs:154-241; 256-entry linear LZ77 lookback at modular/mod.rs:651,1499-1519) but surfaced two findings that overturn the proposed sub-phase order.

Finding A -- 4D (LZ77 hash-chain) is not on the wall-time hot path. greedy_lz77_events is reached only via encode_ans_stream_lz77, called from the Exact price tier and final emit (modular/mod.rs:1291-1295), not the cheap-tier scan loop. The session's own --diag run confirms the call-count split: exact_prices=3 vs cheap_scores=67 per plan_for call, flat across 256/1024/2048px sizes (topology-driven, not size-driven). The 33.5s modular wall is dominated by the 67 full-plane cheap residual scans (6 predictors x greedy split grid over SPLIT_PROPERTIES x SPLIT_THRESHOLDS + per-leaf refinement, lossless.rs:154-248), not LZ77 search cost. 4D is a modest density lever at best (helps only where a copy is already adopted, C.3.3 gate at modular/mod.rs:1361) and moves neither the wall-time nor the 118x density number materially -- demoted to an optional tail item.

Finding B -- 4A (Weighted/H.5 predictor) is far cheaper than scoped. The decoder already has a complete, tested clean-room implementation: crates/jpxl-decode/src/modular/weighted.rs (WeightedState::predict/update, max_error as property 15), invoked per-sample at jpxl-decode/src/modular/mod.rs:684-710. 4A is not "invent H.5," it is "mirror the decoder's working state machine on the encode residual path": add Predictor::Weighted=6 (must match decoder's enum index) and add property 15 to SPLIT_PROPERTIES (currently [4,5,6,7,9,10,11] at lossless.rs:81, missing 15). The only correctness hazard is byte-exact wrap/narrow arithmetic parity with the decoder (jpxl-decode/mod.rs:706-710) -- caught by the existing round-trip gate.

Corrected order: 4.0 (done, this session -- diag re-confirms 2026-08-06 numbers, no regression from S8-era VarDCT-only changes) -> 4.0b (NEW, zero-risk: pinned real-corpus density + decode-validity gate, see jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-0b-density-gate) -> 4A -> 4C -> 4B -> 4D (optional tail).

Rationale for reordering ahead of 4B: the project's optimization-determinism-contract requires Contract-B changes (deliberately altering encoder decisions -- 4A and 4C both do) to name metric bounds in an explicit revise; bounds cannot be named without a working density-measurement harness, which does not yet exist (jpxl-conformance/src/metrics.rs has pixel-error helpers only, no bpp/size-ratio helper). 4B (sampled property-gather) is a pure search-speed optimization -- the existing exact final-price gate (lossless.rs:259-306, PriceTier::Exact) already guarantees the emitted bytes are exactly priced regardless of how the search reached that candidate, so 4B does not block on density measurement and can follow once 4A/4C establish whether the model-strength gap is the real remaining cost.

See also (prior scoping context, cited in prose since assessment cannot target work records via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped, jpegxl-rs.assessment.s8-close-phase4-reorient, jpegxl-rs.assessment.encoder-architecture-outside-advice (source of the original, not-yet-refreshed-on-real-corpus 118x density claim that 4.0b exists to make live and reproducible).

### Advisor design: wire Weighted via sweep+refinement only, sequential collector, no property-15 split, four-part correctness gate

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4a-weighted-integration-design/1`

An independent Opus advisor review of jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4a-weighted-predictor-scoped (run against live code) gave an actionable design, subsequently implemented and verified (jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-weighted-predictor-wired-2026-08-08).

1. Placement: Weighted enters only via the single-leaf predictor sweep and per-leaf refinement (both already loop over PREDICTOR_CANDIDATES), NOT the greedy split search's inner loop. split_leaf always carries the parent leaf's chosen predictor forward unchanged ('same predictor both sides first'), so a Weighted-winning sweep result propagates into splits for free without the split loop needing its own Weighted branch.

2. Cost bound (advisor corrected the original framing): pricing any Weighted-containing tree requires a full sequential O(pixels) scan (sampling would desync the H.5 error state; the specialised single-leaf fast paths don't apply either). If Weighted wins the sweep, EVERY split-round candidate becomes Weighted-on-both-sides, meaning up to rounds x leaves x |SPLIT_PROPERTIES| x |SPLIT_THRESHOLDS| sequential scans, not the '1 + num_leaves' bound the original scoping assumed -- bounded in practice by DEEP_SEARCH_SAMPLE_CAP (large frames cap to one split round). Recommended measuring wall-time impact before committing further; not yet done as a formal A/B in this pass (deferred -- see note below).

3. Property 15 (max_error): deliberately excluded from SPLIT_PROPERTIES for this sub-phase. Confirmed a pure encoder-side search-cost decision with zero effect on decode behaviour or bitstream legality -- the decoder always runs WeightedState unconditionally regardless of what the encoder's search considers, and WPHeader is unconditionally present in every sub-bitstream per H.2 regardless of whether predictor 6 is used anywhere.

4. Correctness gate: sharing jpxl_core::modular_weighted makes the H.5.2 arithmetic question vacuous (same code both sides), but call-site parity (how each crate builds SelfCorrectingNeighbours, and whether the state advances correctly on every sample including non-Weighted-leaf samples in a mixed tree) is NOT vacuous and is the live risk. Gate implemented: forced single-leaf and mixed-tree round trips through jpxl-decode, an independent djxl oracle round trip (catches shared-module-vs-spec bugs a same-crate round trip cannot), and a multi-section round trip verifying WeightedState resets at group boundaries (all passing).

Deferred from this pass, per advisor's own conditional recommendation ('implement the simple version... run the gate, add mitigation only if the time gate trips'): the formal 2x/3x wall-time A/B gate and the surrogate-seeded topology mitigation. Implementation landed with correctness fully gated; the performance-regression risk flagged in point 2 above is a known open item, not yet measured on a large-frame Weighted-seeded corpus case.

See also (prose citation, assessment cannot target work via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4a-weighted-predictor-scoped, jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-weighted-predictor-wired-2026-08-08.

### Advisor reorientation: S8 closes as honest negative; Phase F no-go; next round is Phase 4 (modular, density-first)

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.s8-close-phase4-reorient/1`

Independent Opus-advisor review, checked against the actual code and AKR ledger rather than accepted at face value, on the question of where encoder optimization work should go after S8's closure.

Verification of the S8 closure holds up: the s8-cover-prune Cargo feature is confirmed not in default; cheap_stage_would_prune and all its call sites in lib.rs are #[cfg(feature = "s8-cover-prune")]; the measured net slowdown (+20-25% cover_ms) is consistent with cell_lower_bound's scalar loop losing to choose_lane4's SIMD batching. No Phase 4/5/6 AKR work items exist yet -- confirmed greenfield at the ledger level.

Correction to the pre-review framing: outside-advice.md §14's modular diagnosis is partly stale. Phase 1 (not just VarDCT-focused work) already fixed modular's cheapest problems -- plane deep-clones eliminated via Arc<[i32]> score-plane sharing (lossless.rs, ~10GiB->432MB at 12MP, wall ~44s->33.5s, byte-identical), specialized single-leaf residual kernels (modular/mod.rs West/North/Gradient fast paths), and cheap-vs-exact trial pricing (PriceTier::Cheap for search, PriceTier::Exact only on settled finalists). What remains from §14-15 is model-strength, not raw copy/interpretation cost: no Weighted predictor (lossless.rs, deferred), local-only MA trees (use_global_tree=false, no global histogram clustering), full-image cheap-tier trial scans (no sampled/summarized gather per §15), and a naive 256-entry linear LZ77 lookback with no cheap repetition gate.

A second correction: post-Phase-1-3, VarDCT's fattest 12MP stage is now entropy (3.68s of 8.3s total) not cover (1.79s) -- relevant to ruling out Phase F, since even a working within-probe cover prune would only target a ceiling of ~3% of VarDCT wall.

Phase F (S8's aggressive closed-form/continuous rate-estimate half) verdict: FIRM NO-GO. Four independent reasons: its own within-probe predecessor (Phase D) measured a net loss; the realistic ceiling is now tiny given entropy is the fat stage; CfL's closed-form-from-sufficient-statistics estimate was already tried and reverted twice at a smaller, safer decision surface (see phase2-cfl-quant evidence); and cover selection is a larger, more consequential surface where the same failure mode is more likely, not less.

Next-round recommendation: Phase 4 (rebuild modular planning), reframed density-first rather than a from-scratch rebuild, since the cheap speed wins are already banked by Phase 1. Justification: modular is the largest remaining absolute cost (33.5s vs VarDCT's 8.3s at 12MP, ~4x), the least-addressed gap proportionally (~22% wall reduction from one phase vs VarDCT's ~45% from three), has the worst density benchmark point on record (~118x slower at e1 for essentially identical output size -- a model-strength failure, not a speed one), and is the safest major rebuild available in this codebase because lossless gives an exact-pixel-identity oracle for every sub-phase with no Butteraugli/perceptual-calibration dependency (unlike further VarDCT work, which needs Phase 5 first). Phase 6 (entropy, the fattest VarDCT stage) is the strongest VarDCT-side alternative but outside-advice.md §20 deliberately orders low-level entropy work last, after architecture reshaping; Phase 5 (perceptual parity) is a prerequisite for judging VarDCT density honestly but is calibration-heavy and blocked on a §19 corpus with provenance sidecars that doesn't exist yet (test-set/ still violates AGENTS.md §9, tracked at S8's deferred Phase E).

Scoping sketch handed to jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase4-modular-scoped follows the same measure-before-design, prove-safety-before-wiring, honest-negatives-acceptable discipline S8 and phases 1-3 used: 4.0 re-measure the current (post-Phase-1) modular baseline by stage so no sub-phase re-solves what Phase 1 already fixed; 4A Weighted predictor (density, exact-lossless-safe -- byte size is the only oracle needed since lossless can't be "wrong", only bigger); 4D LZ77 gating via a cheap repetition estimate ahead of the full alternative encode (speed, output-preserving, byte-identity gate); 4B sampled property-gather replacing full-image cheap-tier trial scans (the invasive piece -- proven against the full-scan scorer on fixtures before wiring, same discipline as S8's regret-harness pattern, honest-negative-acceptable if winner selection drifts too far); 4C global/chunk-global tree + histogram clustering (density, interacts with the entropy stage so scoped separately). Suggested order 4.0 -> (4A + 4D) -> 4B -> 4C, front-loading the cheap/safe wins.

See also (precedent/context, cited in prose since assessment cannot target work records via supported_by): jpegxl-rs.work.arch-s8-full-redesign-scoped (the closed S8 line this reorients from), jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase3-forward-cache (established the 96-97% cross-probe forward reuse this builds on), jpegxl-rs.observation.preopt-flamegraphs-2026-08-06 (pre-opt baseline flamegraphs).

### Semantic guidance is an optional quality prior, not the parity architecture

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.semantic-guidance-is-a-quality-prior-not-parity-architecture/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/field.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/rate.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/src/**"`

Phase 8.6 rejects raw coefficient-residual allocation as a sufficient perceptual signal: its isolated Butteraugli-max gains traded against SSIMULACRA2 or pnorm3 and its fifth exact candidate was materially slower. The sibling bpg-rs implementation reinforces the distinction: cheap local edge, contrast and noise saliency is a heuristic used for search steering, while its reliable AQ path measures an actual uniform encode and may run a third equal-rate candidate gate because source statistics do not predict the winner. raw-autotune exposes a versioned codec-neutral 8x8 semantic confidence map for sky, vegetation and building or interior uses and explicitly leaves quantizer direction, strength and compensation to the encoder; that can become an optional JPXL quality prior after corpus validation. It does not reduce the current 4.57 to 6.03 times runtime gap and cannot replace structural traversal or parallelism work. Because raw-autotune is AGPL-3.0-or-later while JPXL is MIT OR Apache-2.0, JPXL must not directly depend on or copy its implementation absent an explicit relicensing or legal decision; use an independently authored neutral input contract with adaptation in raw-autotune or a process or sidecar boundary.

- `#license-boundary` — The JPXL side may define and consume its own generic guidance contract but cannot take a direct AGPL implementation dependency under its current licensing.
- `#measured-residual-negative` — A measured high-frequency residual by itself does not distinguish important structure from expendable texture or noise.
- `#semantic-guidance-role` — Scene semantics can seed or constrain allocation and candidate search, but promotion still requires equal-rate multi-metric measurements and default byte identity.
- `#speed-track-separate` — Semantic inference and AQ candidate comparison are outside the encoder speed-parity denominator unless separately reported; the next main checkpoint remains profile-justified structural work.

### Surrogate navigation does not pay for wall even at 0.4× probe cost

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.surrogate-navigation-does-not-pay-for-wall/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-plan-render/**"`

Measured twice on both reserved holdouts: with the interim shrink-after-reconstruct surrogate (~0.6× a canonical probe, S1) and with the S2 decimating render (0.398×, flat across image sizes), the navigator's bracket-acquire-plus-canonical-confirm structure spends ~1.5–2 surrogate probes per canonical probe it saves, leaving engaged-cell wall at ~1.00–1.01 despite cutting canonical metric evaluations 27–31% on engaged cells. Two structural facts bound the win: post-N3 canonical searches in the routable band are already short (~2.6 probes at target 90), and a surrogate probe's irreducible cost is the pixel plan plus the full-resolution varblock reconstruction — decimation only removes restoration, colour and metric work. The surrogate-navigation feature therefore stays off by default, and the rest of N3's routing table that waited on cheap surrogates stays parked. A genuine flip would need a coefficient-domain decimated reconstruction (~0.2× or less, IDCT folded with the 2:1 box average), which is a new phase decision with its own recalibration, not a tuning of the existing machinery.

### The advisor's 1.5-probe target is predictor-bound; the navigator-side ceiling is about -0.45 to -0.6 probes per encode under Contract B

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.assessment.two-probe-path-is-predictor-bound-2026-09-02/1`

The deterministic two-probe common case the 2026-09-01 advisor pack ranks second (predicted crossing, one direct correction, certified stop, old navigator on exceptions) cannot reach the advisor's target of <= 1.5 mean canonical pixel probes and <= 2 probes for 90% of in-domain requests on the current 95-fixture corpus, whatever slope it corrects with: the replay of 2026-09-02 shows a corrected stop lands inside the existing one-point band 79% of the time only when the first probe is already within 0.25 ln scale of the crossing and never beyond 1.0, and only 37% of the corpus's non-in-band first probes are that close (median 0.32, p90 1.38). The binding quantity is therefore the first-probe predictor's log-scale error, which would need a p90 near 0.25 on this corpus; the 2026-09-02 all-knot retrain measured a blind p90 of 1.854. Until a predictor of that accuracy exists (or the corpus stops being dominated by the 28 saturated and tiny synthetic cells that are both worst-predicted and least simulable), the 1.5-probe target should not be pursued through navigator changes, and 'class-aware routing' on this corpus routes text-screenshot, grayscale, noise and photo-scene cells (already 1.7-2.0 probes with the corrected stop) while leaving saturated and gradient cells, which carry most of the probes, on the exact path. What the navigator side can still buy under Contract B is bounded and now quantified: (1) the corrected stop with a 0.5 ln-scale move gate, trusted in-band first probes and one second correction, worth about -0.45 probes per encode on the corpus (-0.55 in-domain), byte-neutral in geometric mean (0.998-1.001) with a fair overshoot no worse than the deployed path, tail +9% in-domain, about 5-6% of probe wall on the >= 4 MP cells; the ungated form reaches -0.6 probes and about 10% of probe wall but carries a +30% fallback-budget tail and a worse overshoot, so a move gate is part of any promotable form; (2) replacing the legacy ladder-ceiling start (rung 73727) for log2_pixels-flagged large photos with the flagged model median, which by the trace would remove two expansion probes on each 12 MP photo cell. Both alter which rung wins and need the operator's Contract B decision, a feature-gated implementation, and the standing one_shot_promotion_ab.py corpus gate (floor, byte geo-mean, per-cell tail, byte identity across threads) before promotion; neither is a 2x lever. This assessment rests on an offline replay with interpolated counterfactual scores and unpinned per-probe millis, so the probe counts are the claim, not the wall figures.

### One documented command compares JPXL and native cjxl/djxl on the same inputs with recorded provenance

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.bench-vs-libjxl-reproducible-2026-08-25/1`

### ROW_LANES 8 to 6 in the horizontal blur is byte-identical and cuts Balanced quality wall 2.8-3.9% on both anchors

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.blur-row-lanes-register-pressure-2026-08-31/1`

One horizontal-blur recursion step keeps six live [f64; ROW_LANES] arrays (prev and prev2 per pole, plus sum and acc). At the previous ROW_LANES=8 that is twelve of AVX2's sixteen ymm registers before addressing, loads or the f32 conversion, and the state spilled to the stack every sample: the instruction mix of horizontal_band_avx2, the encoder's top leaf at 14.1% of wall, was 25.9% stack spill/fill, 21.9% shuffle, 16.7% scalar-double FP and only 9.6% vector work. A first fix that gave pole_step fixed-size array parameters instead of slices changed the mix by less than a point and was reverted -- inline(always) had already exposed the lengths, so slice erasure was not the mechanism. Sweeping the lane count with the in-tree row_lanes_bench (4000-wide band, ns/sample, plane/product) gave 2: 2.06/2.18, 4: 1.99/2.15, 6: 1.66/1.98, 8: 2.65/2.62, 12: 2.63/2.74, 16: 3.36/3.40 -- a sharp non-monotonic optimum at 6, worth -37.6% plane and -24.6% product against the shipped 8. Making horizontal_padded_lanes lane-count-generic (it previously spelled out eight outputs) was separately measured as neutral at 8 lanes, so the win is the lane count alone. End-to-end three-arm A/B through JPXL/tools/quiet_ab.py, pinned to the six physical P-cores, ABBA-interleaved, 12 repetitions, percentile-bootstrap CI on the paired ratio: ROW_LANES=6 versus HEAD gives 0.9685 [0.9583, 0.9780] at 4.3 MP t4, 0.9606 [0.9499, 0.9794] at 4.3 MP t6, 0.9702 [0.9586, 0.9836] at 12 MP t4 and 0.9725 [0.9677, 0.9837] at 12 MP t6 -- four of four FASTER with every interval excluding 1.0. ROW_LANES=4 is materially weaker (0.988-0.995), matching the microbench ordering. Codestreams are byte-identical. Wall moves less than the kernel because horizontal_band is 14.1% of wall and BAND_ROWS=64 leaves a four-row remainder per band on the scalar path at six lanes; routing that remainder through a narrower lane group is the obvious follow-up. Measured on a thermally saturated host (96 C, 1050-1920 MHz, load ~3.5), which the harness reports: the effect is far outside the harness's demonstrated noise floor of about 0.5%, established by a null A/B of the release binary against a copy of itself returning 1.0004 [0.9922, 1.0052].

### E1-a retested on a quiet pinned host buys 8.9-10.2% at 12 MP for 2.36 GiB, not the ~6% the closure recorded

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.e1a-retention-retest-quiet-2026-08-31/1`

E1-a (reference::LOW_MEMORY_PIXELS 8 MP to 24 MP, retaining the source-side blurred moments at 12 MP) was closed 2026-08-30 on a loaded-host reading of -4..-6% wall against the operator's ~10% bar for the relaxed 2.2-2.5 GB memory envelope. Retested on an idle host (3.2% CPU busy at the start; load average is not a usable idleness gate here because the repo's ntfs-3g FUSE mount parks tasks in D state and reads 1.5-2.0 when idle), pinned to the six physical P-cores, ABBA-interleaved, 16 repetitions, per-child peak RSS via os.wait4, stacked on top of the ROW_LANES=6 blur fix: 12 MP t4 ratio 0.8985 [0.8842, 0.9102] and 12 MP t6 0.9111 [0.8999, 0.9219] against unmodified HEAD, both intervals excluding 1.0. Isolating E1-a from the lane fix by dividing the two candidate arms gives roughly -8.0% (t4) and -5.8% (t6) for E1-a alone, so the combined -10.2%/-8.9% is what actually clears the bar. Peak RSS at 12 MP is 2396 MiB (t4) and 2416 MiB (t6) against a 1979 MiB baseline: +417/+438 MiB, landing at 2.34-2.36 GiB, inside the operator's stated 2.2-2.5 GB envelope. The 4.3 MP anchor is unaffected as expected (4.32 M pixels never crossed the old 8 MP threshold, so both arms take the same path: 0.9830 and 0.9652, statistically the lane fix alone). Codestreams byte-identical. This does not by itself promote E1-a: it re-opens the trade the 2026-08-30 closure decided against, on a measurement the closure could not have made, and the memory-12mp acceptance check on @jpegxl-rs.work.pqc-usable-efforts-cost still states a 2.0 GB cap that this would breach and that the operator would have to renegotiate explicitly.

### Removing EPF's per-access bounds checks does not pay — the 35% scalar int/control share is not bounds checking

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.epf-bounds-check-removal-negative-2026-08-31/1`

After the inv_sigma hoist, epf_step_rows_fma still measured 34.7% of its cycles as scalar integer and control instructions against 30.5% ymm, which read as a bounds-checking profile: the pixel loop issued roughly ninety checked accesses per pixel (d.get(x) per tap, rows3.get(c).and_then(|r| r.get(x)) per tap per channel, acc.get(c) and plane.get_mut(idx) per channel). The tested change trimmed every row the loop reads to exactly `width` once per row via .get(..width), replaced the enumerate-plus-get channel walks with direct zips, and indexed directly under an #[allow(clippy::indexing_slicing)] with a justification, on the grounds that x is bounded by width and the output index by the already-validated out.len() == width * rows.len(). jpxl-core's 159 tests passed and clippy was clean after rewriting one let-else as ?. Wall, pinned ABBA A/B at 16 repetitions: 0.9948 [0.9917, 1.0041] at 4.3 MP t4, 0.9956 [0.9820, 1.0064] at 4.3 MP t6, 0.9981 [0.9890, 1.0106] at 12 MP t4, 0.9931 [0.9878, 1.0084] at 12 MP t6 -- four of four INCONCLUSIVE, every interval spanning 1.0. All four point the same direction, so a real effect near 0.5% cannot be excluded, but that is at or under the harness's demonstrated resolution and well under the effect sizes this programme has been landing. The conclusion is that the scalar int/control share is loop control and index arithmetic that LLVM had already handled, not bounds checks. Reverted: the change bought nothing measurable while adding an indexing_slicing allow and direct indexing to a kernel shared by the decoder and the plan renderer. Recorded so the profile share is not read this way again. The instruction-mix share moved the wrong way when measured (34.7% to 45.7% int/control), which is consistent with the symbol's other work shrinking rather than the integer work growing, and is a reminder that within-symbol shares cannot rank a change on their own.
