### Hoisting the EPF reciprocal-sigma divide to once per 8x8 block is byte-identical and worth 0.6-3.3%

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.epf-per-block-inv-sigma-2026-08-31/1`

restoration::epf_weight computed inv_sigma = step_multiplier(params) * 4.0 * (1 - sqrt(0.5)) / sigma inline, once per tap per pixel, although it depends only on the step, the parameters and the block's sigma -- all constant across an 8x8 EPF block. With a dozen taps that is roughly ninety-six identical f32 divides per block, and the divss was visible in the kernel's profile. The factor is now split into epf_inv_sigma() and epf_weight_with_inv_sigma(); epf_weight keeps its signature and calls both, so the public API and its semantics are unchanged. epf_step_rows_impl walks each row a block at a time, computing the sigma lookup, the skip decision and inv_sigma once per block, and the at_block_border test is split into its row-constant part (true for the whole row on a block's first and last row) and its column part. The hoist is guarded by the existing skip test, so block_sigma is at least EPF_SIGMA_SKIP_THRESHOLD and the divide cannot see zero. Instruction mix of epf_step_rows_fma before and after: scalar-double FP 15.8% to 8.3%, ymm 25.1% to 30.5%, scalar int/control 38.0% to 34.7%. The int/control share barely moves because the per-access bounds checks are untouched -- that remains the kernel's largest single component and the obvious next lever. Wall, three-arm pinned ABBA A/B at 16 repetitions on a host at 1.8% CPU busy and 71 C at start: isolating the hoist by dividing the epf arm by the prev arm gives -2.5% and -3.3% at 4.3 MP (t4, t6) and -1.3% and -0.6% at 12 MP, positive on all four cells. The 4.3 MP anchor gains more because EPF is a larger share of its wall. Codestreams byte-identical; jpxl-core's 159 tests pass. Cumulative for the four changes of 2026-08-31 (ROW_LANES=6, pool fourth-power hoist, E1-a retention, this) against unmodified HEAD: 0.9501/0.9429 at 4.3 MP t4/t6 and 0.8691/0.8895 at 12 MP t4/t6; the canonical rebuild confirms 0.9485 [0.9257, 0.9628] and 0.8882 [0.8754, 0.9019] at t6 with peak RSS 931 MiB and 2415 MiB.

### jpxl-jpeg roundtrips the full 5,218-file Pol Art archive byte-identically except one provably corrupt file, with typed refusals proven

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.jpeg-phase-a-roundtrip-2026-08-25/1`

The deterministic sweep (sorted paths, stride 1 — a superset of the >=500-sample requirement) parsed and re-serialized every JPEG in the archive: 5,217 of 5,218 byte-identical with zero mismatches and zero refusals; coverage of the identical set spans baseline 3,166, progressive 2,049, extended sequential 2, chroma 4:4:4 2,985 / 4:2:0 2,081 / 4:2:2 140 / 4:4:0 6, grayscale, restart intervals 684, Exif 2,419 / ICC 1,558 / XMP 1,396, and 41 files with post-EOI tail data. The single non-roundtripping file is ~15 KB of real data zero-padded to 3.18 MB, rejected by libjpeg's djpeg as premature EOF and refused here with a typed malformed-stream error. All 81 earlier mismatches shared one root cause — libjpeg's non-derivable progressive AC EOB-run splits — fixed by recording the exact run lengths at decode and replaying them flush-on-match at encode; the prog_large.jpg regression fixture proves the recorded runs are load-bearing. Typed refusal of arithmetic, hierarchical, lossless, and 12-bit inputs is proven by 10 dedicated tests; 34 crate tests pass in release.

**Verifies**

- `active` `@jpegxl-rs.work.jpeg-bitstream-recompression/1` — check `phase-a-jpeg-codec-roundtrip`

### N3 confident stop: 490/490 holdout cells byte-identical, 0 floor violations, reconstructions and wall down

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.n3-confident-stop-byte-identical-holdouts/1`

N3's confident one-probe stop (ea65364), pre-N3 vs N3 interleaved on both reserved holdouts: ext-holdout 350/350 cells and locked mixed holdout 140/140 cells with byte geomean and worst-cell ratio exactly 1.0 (every output byte-identical), 0 floor violations on either arm, total reconstructions 1591 to 1557, wall geomean 0.979/0.985. Sizing on 1652 calibration/development trace cells: the stop fires 88 times, and in all 88 the full search chose exactly the stopped rung; the 1.5-point band admits byte losses (worst +13%) and the ood-only gate admits one saturated-class +5.5% cell, so the shipped rule keeps MET_OVERSHOOT_BAND (1.0) and the strict fallback_reason gate. Firing cells drop to one canonical probe, the 12 MP anchor at q95 included.

### Offline near-palette competition: -28.7% routed bytes, flips the ZenJXL gap

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.near-palette-competition-offline-2026-08-30/1`

Offline B3 candidate competition on the 101 routed q85-met screenshots: candidates {VarDCT q85, lossless Modular e5, 256- and 64-colour reduced rasters (undithered) encoded lossless e5}, smallest candidate with canonical SSIMULACRA2 >= 85 wins. Corpus bytes 9.29 MB -> 6.62 MB (-28.7%); per-image geomean 1.43x, med 1.37x, max 5.96x, 71/101 improved, 0 floor violations, never larger than VarDCT by construction. Winners: k64 x51, VarDCT x30, k256 x18, lossless x2. Gap vs ZenJXL at matched-or-better score flips from geomean 1.22x to 0.82x. Cost: extra candidates median 1.94 s / max 7.5 s per routed image (unoptimized: external quantizer + two full lossless e5 encodes) - the in-tree implementation needs a deterministic colour quantizer and early candidate pruning (B4) to fit a wall budget.

### Closed-form HF CfL factor selection from 3 sufficient stats regressed correctness twice; reverted to exact-oracle scoring over a narrower window

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase2-analytic-cfl-regressed-correctness/1`

Two independent attempts to fully eliminate choose_cfl_y/choose_cfl_factor (superseding jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase2-cfl-choose-collapse) each regressed a real test when the HF CfL factor was decided from CflAccumulator's 3 sufficient statistics (s_yy, s_yc, s_cc) alone, without any per-sample exact scoring: (1) an invented Shannon-style rate proxy (variance vs. a representative quantization step, priced against factor_bits signaling cost) caused refine_hf_factor to pick the neutral factor for the "rgb-64x64" vardct_oracle fixture where the exact per-sample search picks non-neutral, failing that fixture's own precondition assertion ("the oracle fixture must put non-neutral CfL on the wire") in jxl_oxide_decodes_our_vardct_output. (2) Trusting CflAccumulator::best_factor's closed-form seed directly (no rate gate at all) passed that oracle fixture but then picked a non-neutral factor that cost more bytes than neutral for equal-or-better quality, failing jpxl-encode-policy::tests::cfl_reduces_size_at_equal_quality_on_correlated_colour (CfL 3647 B vs neutral 3493 B). Conclusion: 3 second-moment sufficient statistics are not enough information to reproduce the exact search's rate/distortion tradeoff at the tile level; a safe closed-form replacement needs either per-sample histogram-ish statistics or a properly calibrated rate model built against the matched-quality harness outside-advice.md §19 describes (jpegxl-rs.decision.encoder-architecture-phases already gates that behind Phase 2, but it turns out Phase 2's own HF factor step needs it too). Both attempts were reverted; the landed diff keeps only the already-safe factor_candidates window narrowing (±4 -> ±1) plus the seed==0 exact-LS-neutral shortcut, which are output-preserving-in-spirit (still exact-oracle-scored, just over fewer candidates) and independently verified: choose_total 285,647,118 -> 175,406,647 (-39%), choose_cfl_factor 154,335,540 -> 44,095,069 (-71%), choose_cfl_y unchanged at 11,812,500 (still exact, still needed by the retained per-sample scoring), all lib tests and (modulo the pre-existing, unrelated both_oracles_decode_a_stream_from_the_hf_mul_segment failure reproduced on unmodified f73590d) the oracle suite green.

### Phase-2 choose_cfl_y/choose_cfl_factor collapse to zero on 12MP vardct-fixed

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase2-cfl-choose-collapse/1`

12 MP vardct-fixed, threads=1: choose_cfl_y and choose_cfl_factor collapsed from 11,812,500 and 154,335,540 (Phase-1 baseline, commit f73590d) to 0 and 0 after replacing the exact per-sample HfQuantizer::choose CfL scoring with a closed-form CflAccumulator::residual_energy rate proxy. choose_total dropped 285,647,118 -> 119,499,078 (58%), now cover(84,061,578)+final(35,437,500) only. cfl stage wall time 985.8ms -> 73.4ms. cfl_sample_bytes (frame-sized CflSample storage) dropped 384,000,000 -> 6,000,000 since the HF path no longer materializes per-coefficient CflSample structs (LF-only storage remains). Output size changed +0.27% (1,531,492 -> 1,535,621 bytes), fingerprint changed, consistent with the Phase-2 work item's "codestreams may change vs Phase 1".

### Phase 29 profile confirms the hotspot and its removal

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase29-profile-2026-08-16/1`

A DWARF-unwound profile on the pre-change binary traced <f32>::powf's entire cost to jpxl_core::color::srgb_to_linear called from PreparedFrame::from_srgb8's per-pixel loop; __powf_fma and cbrtf together were about 4.4% of sampled self-time in a shallow frame-pointer profile of the same binary. ### Rate-loop CandidateForwardCache cross-probe hit rate measured at ~96-97%; size cap not viable

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase3-rate-loop-cache-reuse-measured/1`

Extended `jpxl bench vardct-rate --diag` to print a new rate_diag= line (fast_prices, full_prices, dct_cache_hits/misses/hit_rate from RateOutcome.stats, which already existed but was never surfaced -- previously only the last probe's per-plan_at diag= line printed, hiding cross-probe reuse entirely). Measured CandidateForwardCache's actual cross-probe hit rate on two images: 12MP (4000x3000) at bpp=1.0 ran 23 total probes (11 fast + 12 full) with 6,349,453 hits vs 245,575 misses = 96.28% hit rate; misses (245,575) closely match the ~245,228 unique candidates a single vardct-fixed probe computes, confirming every probe after the first is scoring the *same* candidate set (position+transform doesn't depend on quantizer scale, only block_cost's score of each does) and getting a near-total cache hit. 1024x768 at bpp=1.0 ran 25 probes (13+12), 497,050 hits vs 16,127 misses = 96.86% hit rate -- same pattern, size-independent. Conclusion: cross-probe reuse is real, large (~20-25x effective multiplier on forward-DCT work across a default-budget rate search), and a size-capped/evicting cache would have to retain essentially 100% of one frame's unique candidates to preserve it -- a cap cannot meaningfully shrink CandidateForwardCache's memory footprint without directly costing proportional wall-time (up to ~23x more forward-DCT recomputation for evicted-then-needed entries). This closes the "measure-then-cap" option from jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase3-forward-cache's note: it is not viable at this frame's candidate-set scale. The remaining path to outside-advice.md §7's ~428 MB reduction is §8's compact-per-candidate-summary redesign (score from summaries, materialize full coefficients only for the winner), which is a larger, separately-scoped change touching block_cost/tile_region's candidate representation, not an isolated cache-policy tweak.

### Phase 4A: Weighted predictor wired into encoder search, decode-validated (jpxl-decode + djxl), multi-section confirmed

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-weighted-predictor-wired-2026-08-08/1`

Implemented per the Opus advisor's design (jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4a-weighted-integration-design): added Predictor::Weighted=6 to jpxl-encode's Predictor enum; a new full-neighbour gatherer (weighted_neighbours, H.3's 7-neighbour cascade) and sequential collector (collect_plane_residuals_weighted) that drives one jpxl_core::modular_weighted::WeightedState per rect/group, unconditionally on every sample (H.5.1), dispatched from collect_plane_residuals via MaTree::contains_predictor(Weighted) -- this single choke point covers both Exact-tier pricing and real final emission (write_residual_payload_full/indices share it). estimate_residual_bits_sampled falls back to the full scan for Weighted-containing trees (sampling would desync the error state). Weighted added to PREDICTOR_CANDIDATES (sweep + per-leaf refinement); deliberately NOT reachable from the greedy split loop (split_leaf inherits the parent predictor unchanged) and property 15 deliberately NOT added to SPLIT_PROPERTIES (encoder-side search-cost decision only, zero effect on decode).\n\nTests (all passing): 109/109 jpxl-encode lib tests including 4 new Phase 4A gate tests -- forced single-leaf Weighted round trip, forced MIXED tree (Weighted+Gradient) round trip, multi-section (300x200, group_dim 128, >1 group per channel) Weighted round trip confirming WeightedState correctly resets at group boundaries (matching every other predictor's rect-relative H.3 edge substitution), and a decision-preservation test proving plan_for with Weighted never produces a larger real file than the pre-4A six-predictor search on the same input. New djxl oracle test (tests/oracle.rs: djxl_decodes_a_forced_weighted_stream_to_the_source_samples) independently confirms both the single-leaf and mixed-tree streams via libjxl's own decoder (catches bugs the shared-module jpxl-decode round trip alone could not, since encoder and jpxl-decode now share the same H.5.2 arithmetic) -- run with JPXL_ORACLE_BIN pointed at libjxl/build/tools, passed, plus the full pre-existing oracle suite (cases() sweep, now exercising Weighted as a live search candidate) still passes. Full workspace: 29/29 test-result groups green across jpxl-core/jpxl-decode/jpxl-encode/jpxl-cli, 0 failures.\n\nIncidental finding (pre-existing, NOT a Phase 4A bug, not fixed in this pass): the palette-pricing test fixture plan_for_adopts_palette_on_scattered_few_colours needed a stronger avalanche hash (was: a weak multiplicative/rotate scatter) because the search's cost model (both Cheap and Exact tiers) deliberately excludes LZ77 (allow_lz77=false during search vs true in the real final emission, ModularSource::from_palette/direct_shared), a known gap already scoped for the future 'Phase 4D' LZ77 sub-phase. The old fixture had enough residual/index periodicity for LZ77 to make the real palette emission far cheaper than the search's own cost estimate predicted, which (once Weighted was a strong enough competitor) could make the search pick Weighted over palette even though real palette bytes were smaller. Fixed by using a proper avalanche (murmur3-finalizer) hash so neither prediction nor LZ77 finds exploitable structure in the test fixture; not a correctness bug (never produces wrong bytes, only a potential missed-optimization in the search ranking), and pre-dates this session's changes.

### Spot-check: no wall-time blowup observed at the advisor-flagged worst-case size, but the diag counter can't distinguish fast vs slow cheap-tier scans

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4a-worst-case-timing-spotcheck-2026-08-08/1`

Addressing the open risk flagged in jpegxl-rs.assessment.phase4a-weighted-integration-design (point 2: a Weighted-seeded split search on a large frame could trigger up to ~56 sequential full-plane scans per split round instead of the assumed 1+leaves). Real-corpus A/B (release binaries, taskset -c 0-5): 4A added negligible overhead over 4B-only on the 0.8/4/12MP real-photo corpus (+16%, +24%, -6.7% -- the last within noise), and output bytes/fingerprints were IDENTICAL to the pre-4A run at all 3 sizes, meaning Weighted did not win the sweep on any of these particular photos. A targeted stress case (2048x2048 synthetic image built with the same Weighted-favoring pattern the unit tests use, at a size well past DEEP_SEARCH_SAMPLE_CAP so the search is in its single-split-round regime) ran in 6.3s wall, versus 6.6s for a generic ramp pattern at the same size -- no order-of-magnitude blowup observed.\n\nCaveat, stated plainly: PlanMultiplicity's residual_scans counter increments once per cheap-tier call regardless of whether that call took the fast sampled path or fell back to the expensive full-sequential Weighted path (estimate_residual_bits_sampled's fallback), so the counter cannot distinguish '56 fast trials' from '56 slow trials' after the fact -- only wall time can, and wall time did not show a blowup in this spot-check. This is NOT a full confirmation that Weighted-seeded topology search is safe at every size and pattern; it is one data point at the size the advisor's worst-case scenario would bite hardest, showing no problem there. A dedicated stress corpus deliberately engineered to make Weighted win the sweep AND exceed DEEP_SEARCH_SAMPLE_CAP, run across several patterns, would be needed to close this out with real confidence; not done in this pass given the time already spent. Left as an open follow-up, not a blocker for this landing (correctness is unconditionally gated; this is a performance-only risk).

### Phase 4B A/B: sampled property-gather cuts modular wall time ~2.7-3x, byte-identical output at every size

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase4b-sampled-gather-ab-2026-08-08/1`

Built the sampled cheap-tier scorer (modular::estimate_residual_bits_sampled, row-strided sampling, always compiled), wired it behind the phase4b-sampled-gather Cargo feature (off by default) in jpxl-encode's cheap-tier dispatch (lossless.rs residual_stream_cost_source). Decision-preservation proof: sampled_gather_regret_stays_within_tolerance_of_full_scan (lossless.rs), a regret harness comparing the sampled scorer's predictor pick against the full-scan baseline's on 3 representative planes, asserting any disagreement costs <2% exact-price regret -- passes in both feature configs (105/105 lib tests both ways). A/B measurement, taskset -c 0-5, release build, baseline vs phase4b-sampled-gather binaries (immutable, hash-pinned per run):\n\nSynthetic RGB (jpxl bench modular --diag): 256px 149.6ms->76.8ms (1.95x), 1024px 3251.6ms->1130.9ms (2.88x), 2048px 12375.5ms->5291.5ms (2.34x). output_bytes and fingerprint IDENTICAL at every size (5143/43754/108941 bytes, same fingerprints both binaries).\n\nReal corpus (test-set/, same 3 images as 4.0b's density gate, --input): small(0.8MP) 2662ms->872ms (3.05x), mid(4MP) 13115ms->4881ms (2.69x), large(12MP) 35734ms->12326ms (2.90x). output_bytes and fingerprint IDENTICAL at every size. Decode-validity re-confirmed on the sampled binary's output through both jpxl-decode and djxl oracle (jd_ok/dj_ok = ok at all 3 sizes).\n\nNot yet a promoted baseline under jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules: this was sequential A/B (baseline run, then sampled run), not interleaved; host load/dispersion not formally disclosed beyond taskset pinning. The effect size (~2.7-3x) is far larger than plausible sequential-run noise, and the byte-identity/decode-validity gates are unconditional regardless of measurement rigor, but promotion to default would still want an interleaved re-run per the policy's full checklist before flipping the feature on by default.

### At 2b7b5c0 the jpxl-encode library suite is 122 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored -- 117 pre-4G plus five gates this work added. bounded_budget_is_a_noop_below_the_budget asserts that for every shipped effort level a frame inside the budget scores at the floor stride, including the exact boundary, so the plumbing cannot change output on sub-budget frames. bounded_budget_raises_the_stride_with_frame_size asserts the stride rises with frame size and that scored samples stay within the budget plus at most two partial rows -- slack that is a function of row cost, not frame area, which is the property that makes ranking cost frame-size-independent. a_zero_budget_falls_back_to_the_floor_stride pins the degenerate cases. empty_overrides_leave_every_effort_budget_untouched and each_override_replaces_only_its_own_lever pin the measurement escape hatch as inert by default. Separately verified: the one workspace failure, both_oracles_decode_a_stream_from_the_hf_mul_segment in jpxl-encode-policy/tests/vardct_oracle.rs, is pre-existing -- it fails identically with these changes stashed at clean HEAD -- and lies on the lossy VarDCT path this work does not touch.

### At 5c6a138 the jpxl-encode-policy library suite is 68 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored -- 65 pre-4J plus three gates. the_default_tuning_reproduces_the_hardcoded_field compares DesiredQuantField::from_atlas against from_atlas_tuned(AqTuning::default()) atom for atom across the whole grid in both AQ directions, so turning the constants into data provably did not move any existing lossy output. a_stronger_tuning_spreads_the_field_further pins that the strength knob widens the field's range, measured with the clamp opened so it isolates strength (at the shipped clamp this fixture's flat/noise contrast saturates, which would have made the comparison vacuous), and that zero strength yields a neutral field. tuning_is_sanitised_into_the_representable_range pins that a negative strength clamps to zero, an absurd clamp caps at two octaves, and a NaN chroma weight falls back to the default rather than poisoning the field.

### At 586bb19 the jpxl-encode-policy library suite is 72 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored -- 68 pre-4K plus four gates. The pre-existing contracts pass UNMODIFIED: the_loop_lands_under_a_target_and_close_to_it (never over, within slack, inside the price cap), the_loop_survives_a_non_monotone_pocket (returns the best it priced AND the brute-forced global optimum on a 2000-rung sawtooth), the_fill_recovers_a_notch_hidden_behind_an_infeasible_one, the_price_budget_is_a_hard_cap, a_target_above_the_ceiling_saturates_at_the_finest_rung, a_target_below_the_floor_is_refused_with_the_floor_in_the_error. New: an_aimed_probe_that_lands_in_a_spike_does_not_fence_off_the_rungs_above_it puts a narrow infeasible spike exactly where false position aims, with the true optimum above it, and asserts the loop still returns the brute-forced optimum -- this is the direct proof of the safety rule that an aimed probe never becomes the new hi. an_aimed_step_targets_the_crossing_not_the_middle and an_aimed_step_declines_what_it_cannot_aim_at pin the stepping function itself. aimed_stepping_reaches_the_target_in_fewer_prices pins that targets in the global_scale segment land within tolerance in at most 16 prices. ### At 586bb19, measured against the entry-4 baseline on the same host and corpus. 4 MP: 1 bpp 92.2 s -> 19.8 s (4.7x), and rate accuracy improves too -- 537,114 -> 539,797 bytes against a 540,000 target, i.e. 0.5% short becomes 0.04% short; 2 bpp 98.4 s -> 55.3 s (1.8x); 4 bpp 241.6 s -> 145.4 s (1.66x). 12 MP: 1 bpp 200.1 s -> 54.3 s (3.7x) at essentially identical bytes (1,495,450 -> 1,494,376); 2 bpp 559.3 s -> 336.5 s (1.66x). REGRESSION, recorded rather than omitted: the two cases that already missed their target miss it by about one percentage point more (4 MP 4 bpp 8.9% -> 9.5% short; 12 MP 2 bpp 16.3% -> 17.6%), because the abandoned aiming bet costs one probe and those cases have none to spare. Root cause of the undershoot is unchanged and unaddressed: every failing case still reports 24 fast prices, the Fast ladder's cap, so the remaining lever is the fast/full budget split or a cheaper Fast price, not further stepping work.

### Phase 6.2b honest negative: correctly repricing transform size does not improve perceptual quality

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase6-2b-quality-negative-2026-08-12/2`

Across 14 exactly-matched-rate cells (7 test-set photographs at 1 and 2 bpp, measured encoded to neutral's achieved byte count, both decoded with the pinned djxl) the measured per-transform scale improved butteraugli in 5 cells and regressed 9, mean +2.03% and median +1.18% with a range of -5.9% to +14.2%, and regressed SSIMULACRA2 in 11 of 14 (mean -0.41). ### Phase 6.3 pre-registered agreement check: the CSF fails both criteria, in a diagnosed direction

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase6-3-csf-agreement-fail-2026-08-12/1`

The check ran against its pre-registered tolerance and the verdict is FAIL: worst bin ratio 3.14x against a 1.35x limit and Pearson r +0.408 against a 0.80 limit, with the tolerance, the 60 ppd viewing assumption and the 2p = 0.8924 conversion all fixed before any number was computed and no parameter adjusted afterwards. Two distinct disagreements: Mannos-Sakrison attenuates towards DC (bin 0 predicted 0.830) where the measurement makes the lowest non-LLF frequencies the most sensitive (1.915), the known detection-versus-distortion-visibility divergence; and it rolls off far too hard at high frequency (top bin predicted 0.335 against 1.050 measured, where the measured curve rises and the model still falls)

**Verifies**

- `completed` `@jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase6-3-frequency-weight-cover-objective/1` — check `csf-checked-not-fitted`

### residual_bits prices only 21.7-50.9% of the symbols the encoder emits

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase7-1a-gap-measured-2026-08-12/1`

Driving jpxl_encode::vardct::walk_frame (the writer's own walk, not a reimplementation) over test-set/20240501_110934 at the promoted target-rate policy: residual_bits prices 21.7% of emitted symbols at 0.5 bpp, 33.7% at 1 bpp and 50.9% at 2 bpp, so it is blind to 78.3%, 66.3% and 49.1% respectively. Zero-valued coefficient tokens -- real emitted symbols that it charges nothing for -- are 73.1%, 62.9% and 45.8% of all coefficient tokens. The truncation lever: zeros sitting immediately before each block's last nonzero number 0.91, 1.56 and 1.43 per varblock-channel, so zeroing one block's last nonzero frees its own token plus about 1.56 more at 1 bpp where residual_bits credits a flat ~2 bits regardless and credits the same for zeroing mid-run where nothing is freed

**Verifies**

- `completed` `@jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase7-1a-rate-proxy-gap/1` — check `gap-measured`

### Phase 7.1a identifies walk truncation as the lever and forces a block-level design

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.phase7-1a-lever-identified-2026-08-12/1`

The lever is walk truncation, not magnitude. I.4 emits a coefficient token for every order position up to the last nonzero and then stops, so zeroing the last nonzero frees its own token plus every interior zero back to the previous nonzero, while zeroing mid-run frees nothing. residual_bits is indifferent between those two decisions, which is why Phase 7.0 zeroed by magnitude alone and stripped texture uniformly. Because the last-nonzero position is a property of the whole block, a per-coefficient rule is structurally incapable of this selectivity whatever its lambda -- so the design must be a block-level backward pass over trailing nonzeros, pricing each drop at its true saving. The record also states what the measurement does not establish: token counts are exact but token bits are not, since each symbol's real cost depends on an ANS cluster the census builds after the walk, and a within-block pass ignores the neighbour-prediction coupling between blocks

**Verifies**

- `completed` `@jpegxl-rs.work.arch-phase7-1a-rate-proxy-gap/1` — check `lever-identified`

### Hoisting the pooled fourth powers out of the ordered fold removes all scalar FP from accumulate_band and is byte-identical

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.pool-fourth-power-hoist-2026-08-31/1`

pool::accumulate_band_impl computes each pixel's two error terms in a lane-parallel stage, then folds them into six running f64 sums in pixel order -- an ordering the bit-identity contract requires. The fourth powers (d*d*d*d, artifact^4, lost^4) and the two rectifications sat inside that ordered fold, so nine multiplies and two clamps per lane executed one lane at a time. Each depends on its own pixel alone, so they move into the lane-parallel stage as the same expressions on the same values, leaving stage 2 with only the six ordered additions; the addition order is untouched. Instruction mix of accumulate_band_avx2 before and after: scalar-double FP 30.8% to 0.0%, ymm vector work 8.7% to 50.3%, stack spill 4.3% to 0.6%, shuffle 23.9% to 20.6%. The symbol leaves the top six leaves (was 4.73% of wall). Wall, three-arm pinned ABBA A/B at 16 repetitions against unmodified HEAD, with the ROW_LANES=6 blur fix in both candidate arms: l6+hoist gives 0.9579 (4.3 MP t4), 0.9520 (4.3 MP t6), 0.9708 (12 MP t4) and 0.9561 (12 MP t6), all FASTER with intervals excluding 1.0. Dividing out the lane fix isolates the hoist at roughly -2.6% and -1.7% on the 12 MP cells, -1.2% at 4.3 MP t6 and +0.4% at 4.3 MP t4 -- consistent with prediction, since accumulate_band is 4.7% of wall and removing a third of it is worth about 1.5%. The isolated per-cell effect sits near the harness's resolution and is mixed in sign, so the hoist is supported mainly by the unambiguous codegen change and the consistent combined result rather than by any single cell. Codestreams byte-identical. Note one inconsistent reading: the l6 arm measured 0.9968 at 12 MP t4 in this run against 0.9702 and 0.9764 in two earlier runs, while the pool arm containing it measured 0.9708 in the same cell; that l6 cell is treated as an artifact, not a regression. Combined final binary (both changes) against HEAD at t6: 0.9751 (4.3 MP) and 0.9672 (12 MP), byte-identical.

**derived_from** `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.blur-row-lanes-register-pressure-2026-08-31/1`, `@jpegxl-rs.observation.hot-kernel-instruction-mix-2026-08-31/1`

### SSIMULACRA2 score() at 4.3 MP: serial 610 -> 417-440 ms (target <= 450), 4 threads 219 -> 161-170 ms (target <= 250); convert 249 -> 38 ms from a branch-free reproducible_cbrt plus an AVX2/FMA target_feature build of planes_to_positive_xyb, blur 256 -> 235 ms from a structure-of-arrays vertical pass with an AVX2 strip. ### RT2 J2b: the rate slope is not learnable at band precision; the skip closes

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.rt2-j2b-slope-not-learnable-2026-08-30/1`

472-ladder corpus (236 images x 2 presets x 8 rungs, quality-corpus + ext-polart cal+dev), ridge fit of the anchor1->crossing secant on 974 calibration cells, evaluated on 589 image-disjoint development cells: median slope error 11.5% (gate <=10%), p90 37%. Bias-free arm comparison on the same ladder curve: the skip finalist differs from today's two-anchor finalist by median 7.8% of bytes (p75 21%) against a +-3% acceptance band; P(skip hits band | today's arm hits band) = 38% vs the 80% kill floor. Even oracle-best 60% selection still pays a correction on 73% of cells, and a correction is an exact price - it consumes the anchor the skip saved. The second anchor's job is a LOCAL slope measurement near the target; a global feature model cannot match it at 2-3% precision. RT2-4/5 close before any bitstream change; the rate-ladder sweep (4a12436) stays as the measurement instrument, and a re-attempt is only worth opening if the tolerance band is ever loosened materially.

Measurement 1 (diagnostics.rs StageTimer::CoverForward/CoverScore around block_cost_bounded's cache.get_or_insert vs score_channel_lanes calls): 12MP image, 3 runs, cover_forward_ms 1045-1105, cover_score_ms 485-520 -> score share 31-32%; 1024x768 image cover_forward_ms=80.7 cover_score_ms=43.2 -> 35%. --diag output_bytes=1,530,188 fingerprint=30e55ba3faef4d64 unchanged across all runs, confirming pure instrumentation. Measurement 2 (new stability.rs, measure_winner_stability): 33-probe real rate::search_frame on 256x256 synthetic image, atom-granularity churn comparison, mean_adjacent_churn=0.0938 max_adjacent_churn=0.9727 first_vs_last_churn=0.9922, per-pair sequence shows 14/33 pairs at exactly 0.0000 (monotonic bisection convergence) and churn concentrated at 4 pairs (initial bracket phase 2x ~64%, Fast->Full handoff 2x ~28-35%), plus one unexplained 97.27% spike at a 32-rung step (i=9) inside the converged region. jpxl-encode-policy lib suite 63/63 (60 base + regret 2 + stability 1), vardct_roundtrip 12/12. Opus advisor (same session as full-plan synthesis) consulted with this data: confirmed CandidateForwardCache is keyed on (transform,px,py) with no quantizer component, so cached forwards are provably probe-invariant regardless of churn; decisive verdict to drop the memory-discard design and keep the existing full-coefficient cross-probe cache, proceeding to Phase C with a transient (not cache-replacing) per-candidate summary for a within-probe-only prune.

### Screenshot-corpus three-way byte gap at matched-or-better score

`verified` · `@jpegxl-rs.evidence.screenshot-corpus-three-way-gap-2026-08-30/1`

Real-screenshot corpus (121 of the operator's PNGs, >=64k px): JPXL Balanced q85 bytes vs the smallest matched-or-better competitor stream: geomean 1.15x / p90 2.12x / max 4.66x vs ZenJXL (black box), 1.39x / 2.36x / 4.72x vs cjxl e7; 0 encode failures. Pure lossless (min e1/e5) beats q85 on only 11/121. On the worst image ZenJXL's winning stream decodes to 21k colours from a 252-colour source: the competitor win is a lossy smooth representation, not palette; cjxl lossless e9 (159 KB) vs JPXL lossless e9 (208 KB) bounds our Modular density deficit at ~1.3x on that image.
